title: Moduli of abelian varieties
summary: Results classed as known in the literature and missing from Mathlib, proved here with their own definitions.

modules.title: Theta functions on complex tori: Appell–Humbert data and factors of automorphy
modules.note:
This file defines theta functions on a finite-dimensional complex vector space `V` for a subgroup
`L` and a form `B`. The form has type `ThetaTori.LatticeForm L`, which is `RealComplexForm V`
tagged with `L` and imposes no condition. `B` is real linear in the first argument and complex
linear in the second, and is not assumed hermitian. The file also defines the Riemann form
`E = New.RealComplexForm.riemannForm B`, Appell–Humbert data, twisted translations and the dual
lattice, and proves their first properties. Under the assumption that `L` is a full lattice, it
treats factors of automorphy, positive Riemann forms and theta functions without zeros. Below,
`𝐞 t` is `exp (2πi t)` (`New.coe_fourierChar_eq_exp`).

## Main definitions and results

* `New.RealComplexForm.thetaSpace`: the entire `f` with
  `f (z + l) = χ l * exp (B l z + B l l / 2) * f z` for `l ∈ L`. Products and powers of theta
  functions are theta functions (`New.thetaSpace.mul`, `New.thetaSpace.pow`).
* `New.IsAppellHumbert`: Appell–Humbert data; then `riemannForm B` is integral on `L`
  (`New.IsAppellHumbert.le_dualLattice`).
* `New.RealComplexForm.thetaShift`: translation by `a` twisted by `exp (-(B a z + B a a / 2))`. Two
  of these commute, for Appell–Humbert data, up to `𝐞 (E u v)`
  (`New.IsAppellHumbert.thetaShift_comm`). Those by vectors of the dual lattice
  `New.RealComplexForm.dualLattice` preserve, for such data, the theta functions
  (`New.IsAppellHumbert.thetaShift_mem_of_mem_dualLattice`).

modules.title: Theta functions on complex tori: dimension formula, base points, multipliers
modules.note:
This file treats Appell–Humbert data `(B, χ)` with positive Riemann form `E` for a full lattice
`L` in a finite-dimensional complex space `V`. It proves the convergence of theta series and the
existence of a nonzero theta function. It proves that the square of the dimension of the space of
theta functions equals the index of `L` in its dual lattice, and that the twisted translations by
the dual lattice act irreducibly. It shows that multiples of a positive type have no base point.
It also defines the canonical multiplier and the normalised translations.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.IsAppellHumbert.finrank_sq_eq_relIndex`: for Appell–Humbert data with positive `E`,
  `(dim thetaSpace)² = [dual : L]`, the dimension is positive, and the twisted translations by the
  dual lattice span all endomorphisms of the space of theta functions; so the space is irreducible
  (`New.IsAppellHumbert.thetaSpace_le_of_thetaShift_mem`, `New.IsAppellHumbert.schur_lemma`).
* `New.IsAppellHumbert.exists_mem_thetaSpace_nsmul_apply_ne_zero`: for Appell–Humbert data with
  positive `E` and `n ≥ 2` the theta functions of type `(n B, χ ^ n)` have no common zero.
* `New.ThetaTori.canonicalMultiplier`, `New.ThetaTori.normalizedShift`: a canonical multiplier
  `exp (πi E(b x, x))` for a linear map `b`, and the twisted translations divided by it, which, for
  Appell–Humbert data and `b` with `E (b u) w = E u w - E u (b w)`, obey a Heisenberg law
  (`New.IsAppellHumbert.normalizedShift_normalizedShift`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.RealComplexForm.thetaSpace`: the entire `f` with
  `f (z + l) = χ l * exp (B l z + B l l / 2) * f z` for `l ∈ L`.
* `New.RealComplexForm.thetaShift`: translation by `a` twisted by `exp (-(B a z + B a a / 2))`.
* `New.RealComplexForm.dualLattice`: the `v` in `V` with `E(v, l)` an integer for all `l` in `L`.
modules.literature:
Frobenius' dimension formula and irreducibility of the theta group. Here the statement is
basis-free, with the square of the dimension equal to the index of the lattice in its dual. It is
proved together with irreducibility from a theta kernel on the torus without a symplectic basis, and
the orthogonality relation and the absence of base points follow. Source: G. Frobenius, Über die
Grundlagen der Theorie der Jacobischen Functionen, Crelle 97 (1884); Birkenhake–Lange, Complex
Abelian Varieties, 3.2.7, 4.1.5, 6.4; survey of proofs in D. Bump, A. Pekker, Proc. AMS 130 (2002)
3473–3481.

See also `Lib.Shimura.Uniformisation.AppellHumbert`.

modules.title: Lifts of morphisms to sections of line bundles, and theta structures on abelian schemes
modules.note:
A morphism `f : X' → X` and an isomorphism `f^* L ≅ L'` induce a map on global sections
`Φ : H⁰(L) → H⁰(L')`. Over a local ring `R`, these maps let translations of an abelian scheme act on
sections of a line bundle. For a theta structure on `N` indexed by a group `H`, it also gives a
bound on the exponent of `K([N])`, under further hypotheses.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.IsSectionLift`: `Φ` comes from some isomorphism `f^* L ≅ L'`;
  `New.Variety.IsTranslationLift` is the case of a translation; `New.Variety.coordSection` is the
  `j`-th coordinate section of a linear system.
* `New.Variety.exists_isSectionLift`, `New.Variety.IsSectionLift.picClass_eq`: a lift exists when
  `[L'] = f^* [L]`, and only then.
* `New.Variety.IsTranslationLift.mul`, `New.Variety.IsTranslationLift.pow`,
  `New.Variety.exists_isTranslationLift_iff`: lifts of translations multiply, and the translation by
  `z` lifts to `L`, over a local ring `R`, exactly when the pairing `New.Pic.pairing` of `[L]`
  vanishes on `z` and the identity, that is, when `z` lies in the kernel `K([L])`.
* `New.Variety.IsThetaStructure`: a linear system with coordinates indexed by a group `H`, permuted
  up to a cocycle by lifts of the maps `y ↦ ± y + η s`.
* `New.Variety.IsThetaStructure.pull_eq_of_picClass_eq`: rigidity of theta structures along a
  homomorphism.
* `New.Variety.IsThetaStructure.card_nsmul_eq_zero_of_isTranslationLift`: the order of `H` kills
  every section whose translation lifts to `N`, when `N` is a projective embedding; over a local
  ring these are the sections in `K([N])`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.LineBundle.pull`: the pull-back of the line bundle (U_i, g_ij) along p: Y → X, with cover
  p⁻¹U_i and transition functions p*g_ij.
* `New.LineBundle.IsLinearSystem`: L is a linear system, the model being g_ij = s_j / s_i on
  U_i = {s_i ≠ 0} for sections s_i without common zero.
* `New.HasConstFunctions`: for s : X → S, a function regular on all of X takes equal values at two
  ring-valued points with the same image under s.

modules.title: Uniformisations over an arc: theta coordinates, Weil pairing and extension of maps
modules.note:
Let `A` be an abelian scheme over an arc `O` (`New.ValuativeArc`, a valuation ring with fraction
field `ℂ`). Let `u : V / Λ ≅ A(O)` be a uniformisation (`New.Uniformisation`) with `Λ = u.lattice`,
and let `L` be a linear system whose coordinates are theta functions (`New.HasThetaCoords`).
Sections of `L` are read as functions on `V`. Lifts of translations then act by twisted
translations, and their commutators are given by the Weil pairing. With these tools, an additive map
`s' : V → A'(O)` that kills `Λ` and has theta coordinates is shown to come from a morphism `A ⟶ A'`
over `O`, not only over `ℂ`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.isSeparatingFamily_atGeneric_of_surjective`: the complex points `New.atGeneric` of
  the sections are dense in `A`.
* `New.Variety.thetaEval`, `New.Variety.exists_theta_evaluation`: `H⁰(L)` embeds in the
  functions on `V`, and lifts of translations (`New.Variety.IsTranslationLift`) act by multiples
  of the twisted translations `New.RealComplexForm.thetaShift`.
* `New.Variety.lift_commutator_iff_weil_pairing`: the commutator of two lifts is given by the
  Riemann phase `New.RealComplexForm.riemannPhase`.
* `New.Variety.exists_sections_of_translation_stable`: one scalar puts a finite family of theta
  functions in a stable `O`-module. No orbit of the dual lattice consists only of common zeros.
* `New.Variety.exists_section_of_hasThetaCoords`: a section of `π : A' ⟶ A` through the points
  `s' z`.
* `New.Variety.exists_hom_of_hasThetaCoords`: a homomorphism `A ⟶ A'`, obtained from its graph in
  `A × A'`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.IsAbelianScheme`: a commutative group scheme A over S is abelian if it is smooth and proper
  over S and multiplication by every m ≠ 0 is surjective.
* `New.LineBundle.H0`: The R-module of global sections of L, for a scheme X over R; a section `r`
  has a component `r.val i` (a `New.PointFn`) in each chart `i`.
* `New.IsPosRiemann`: The Riemann form E of B is positive: E(u, iu) > 0 for every u ≠ 0.
* `New.Variety.IsTranslationLift`: The R-linear endomorphism Φ of H⁰(L) is pull-back along the
  translation t_z by the section z followed by some isomorphism t_z^*L ≅ L.
modules.literature:
Known result: Homomorphisms and line bundles of abelian schemes extend from the generic fibre. Here
only maps of complex tori that multiply a theta polarisation by an integer are treated, where the
kernel of the polarisation is killed by a unit of the ring, over any valuation ring of the complex
numbers (not noetherian, any rank). The map and the identity of line bundle classes extend together,
and points extend by properness. Source: S. Bosch, W. Lütkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Néron Models (1990),
1.2/8 and 4.4/1; G. Faltings, C.-L. Chai, Degeneration of Abelian Varieties (1990), I.2.7; L.
Moret-Bailly, Pinceaux de variétés abéliennes, Astérisque 129 (1985), II.3.5.

See also `Lib.Shimura.IntegralModel.UniversalFamily` and `Lib.Shimura.Uniformisation.AppellHumbert`.

modules.title: Eigenquotients for Hecke eigensystems and the Galois representations they cut out. Its head has an overview of the theory.
modules.note:
Let `ρ i` be finitely many finite-dimensional `ℚ_ℓ`-representations of `Γ`, with operators `T i s`
and scalars `θ s` in `ℚ̄_ℓ`. The eigenquotient is the largest quotient of `ℚ̄_ℓ ⊗ ⨁ V i` on which
each `T i s` acts by `θ s`. It is given in a basis by `r : Γ → GL_N(ℚ̄_ℓ)` and maps `F i`. If the
`ρ i` are crystalline, then it is crystalline, and a relation between `T` and Frobenius gives a
polynomial that kills Frobenius on it. Suppose moreover that the `T i s` commute with each other and
with `Γ`, and that `γ : ℚ̄_ℓ → ℂ_ℓ` agrees with `a ∈ Gal(ℚ̄_ℓ/ℚ_ℓ)`. If `u` is not a Hodge–Tate jump
of `r` at `γ`, then some polynomial in `T` that is `1` at the conjugate eigenvalues `a ∘ θ` kills
the vectors of weight `u`. These results are applied to the `ℓ`-adic cohomology of a
`New.Variety.Model` to obtain a Galois representation from a system `θ` of Hecke eigenvalues.

## Overview of this theory

Let `E` be a CM field strictly containing `K₀ = ℚ(√-d)`, with `d ≡ 3` mod 4. Let `v₀` be the base
infinite place of a CM type `Φ` of `E`, and let `𝔑` be a nonzero neat level in `𝓞_E`. A finite place
`w` of `E` over a place `u` of `K₀` is *safe* if `u` is split and prime to `d`, and `𝔑` is prime to
`w` and `ū`. The unitary similitude group, of rank `n ≥ 1`, has signature `(1, n - 1)` at `v₀` and
is definite at the other infinite places.

* `New.Variety.exists_model`: an integral model `Z` of Kuga–Sato type for this group, with level
  covers and the congruence relation at safe places. It lives over a localisation `R ⊆ E` of `𝓞_E`
  whose maximal ideals lie over primes good for the PEL data. The inputs are PEL data
  (`New.Variety.exists_pel`) and a family of abelian schemes over such `R`
  (`New.Variety.ThetaNull.nonempty_universalFamily`), for which no universal property is proved. If
  `E` contains a primitive root of unity of order `7! = 5040`, the PEL data exist for a suitable CM
  type and for every nonzero `𝔑` divisible by an integer `N ≠ 0`, which can be taken prime to any
  given finite set of places.
* `New.Variety.exists_isCoefficientSystem`: let `n` be odd, `κ` a weight, and `Φ` a CM type in which
  `Φ v₀` differs on `K₀` from every other `Φ v`. Take a Hecke eigenform of neat level on the
  definite side, with coefficients in an extension of the weight `κ` to `GL_n(E)` that the theorem
  supplies. At one split place it is of cuspidal type. At another split place it is spherical, and
  there the level is pro-`p` Iwahori, `p` being the residue characteristic of that place. Then its
  Hecke eigenvalues `θ` at safe places occur, in the sense of `New.Variety.OccursInWeight`, in
  weight `z + μ` for each jump `z` of `κ` at `Φ v₀`. The jumps are integers given by `New.jumps`.
  Here `μ ∈ ℕ` does not depend on the form or the level.
* `New.Variety.Model.exists_galois_rep`: let `ℓ` be a prime, `ιℓ : ℂ ≃ ℚ̄_ℓ`, and `θ` a system of
  Hecke eigenvalues at safe places. Let `R` be a localisation of `𝓞_E` at elements prime to the safe
  places. Take a model `Z` over `R` and weights `h ≥ 0` in which `θ` occurs. Then there is a
  continuous `ρ : Gal(Ē/E) → GL_m(ℚ̄_ℓ)` of undetermined dimension `m`; the proof cuts it out of the
  cohomology of `Z`. At safe places `ρ` is unramified or crystalline, and the Hecke polynomial of
  `ιℓ ∘ θ` kills geometric Frobenius. If the place over `ℓ` induced by `ιℓ` and the given embedding
  of `E` into `ℂ` is safe, the jumps (Hodge–Tate weights) of `ρ` at that embedding include the given
  weights. Other embeddings and multiplicities are not controlled.

This theory proves the cases that are used of PEL integral models (Kottwitz) and of the geometric
step in the Galois representations of cuspidal forms on `GL_n` (Shin). A direct comparison of two
finite counts replaces the description of automorphic forms on unitary groups via `GL_n` (Labesse).
No moduli functor is represented, nothing is transferred to `GL_n`, and no dimension is computed
here.

1. `ComplexTheta`, `AbelianScheme`, `ThetaGroup`, `Uniformisation`: theta functions and the complex
   uniformisation.
2. `GoodReduction`, `ThetaNormality`, `ArcExtension`: good reduction along a valuation ring of `ℂ`.
3. `ThetaModuli`, `Deformation`: the closure of the theta-null points of the PEL abelian varieties
   carries a family of abelian schemes and is smooth.
4. `HeckeTower` (the list of properties of a model), `CongruenceRelation`, `IntegralModel`: level
   covers, the congruence relation and the model.
5. `TraceFormula`, `Transfer`: the comparison with the definite unitary group. Last, `Eigenspace`:
   the Galois representation.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.IsEigenQuotient`, `New.Variety.exists_isEigenQuotient`: the definition; existence and
  continuity.
* `New.Variety.IsEigenQuotient.isCrystalline`: `r` is crystalline if the `ρ i` are.
* `New.Variety.IsEigenQuotient.isKilledBy`: a relation between `T` and Frobenius gives a polynomial
  that kills Frobenius on `r`.
* `New.Variety.IsEigenQuotient.exists_sum_baseChange_eq_zero_of_jump_eq_zero`: let the `ρ i` be
  crystalline and the `T i s` commute with each other and with `Γ`. If `u` is not a Hodge–Tate jump
  of `r` at an embedding `γ` given by `a ∈ Gal(ℚ̄_ℓ/ℚ_ℓ)`, some polynomial in `T` that is `1` at
  `a ∘ θ` kills the vectors of weight `u`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Period.IsCrystalline`: T is crystalline: the elements of B⊗T fixed by all of Γ span B⊗T over
  B.
* `New.HasHodgeTateWeight`: The element y of C_p⊗T (over Z_p) has Hodge–Tate weight u:
  (j(g)⊗ρ(g))y = χ(j(g))^(−u)·y for all g in Γ, with χ the cyclotomic character.
* `New.Period.jump`: The multiplicity of the Hodge–Tate jump u at γ: the dimension over Q̄_p (zero
  if infinite) of the space `New.Period.hodgeTateMaps` of forms of weight u: γ-semilinear f :
  T → C_p with f(gx) = χ(g)^(−u)·g f(x) for g near 1.
* `New.Period.IsKilledBy`: The polynomial P over R kills (s, m): T is potentially crystalline and
  P(β_{s,m}) = 0 on B⊗T, the coefficients acting through T.
* `New.Period.linearFrob`: β_{s,m}: a chosen B-linear endomorphism of B⊗T agreeing with φ^m
  j(s) ⊗ ρ(s) on D_pcris(T), if one exists (arbitrary otherwise).
modules.literature:
Known result: Galois representation cut out of cohomology by a Hecke eigensystem, and the
Eichler-Shimura relation. Here the representation is a quotient of total cohomology rather than an
isotypic part. No dimension or semisimplicity is stated, only good reduction, annihilation by the
Hecke polynomial and the occurrence of given Hodge-Tate weights. Source: Deligne, Formes modulaires
et représentations l-adiques, Sém. Bourbaki 355 (1969), Thm 4.9; Harris and Taylor, The geometry and
cohomology of some simple Shimura varieties (2001), ch. VII; Wedhorn, Congruence relations on some
Shimura varieties, J. reine angew. Math. 524 (2000).

modules.title: Abelian schemes: base change, finite kernels and constant functions
modules.group: Abelian schemes over a base and their isogenies
modules.note:
This file sets up abelian schemes over a base `S` in terms of `T`-points `T ⟶ A` in `Over S`,
written additively. It shows how points, sections and `O`-linear homomorphisms pass to a base
change. It proves that the kernel of a finite homomorphism into a separated commutative group scheme
over `Spec R` is `Spec S` for a finite `R`-algebra `S` (`New.Variety.exists_finite_kernel_ring`). It
also proves that global functions on the base change of an integral abelian scheme over a field to
an affine base are constant on the fibres (`New.Variety.hasConstFunctions_of_isPullback`).

## Main definitions and results

* `New.AddObj`, `New.ModuleObj O`: commutative group objects, and actions of a ring `O` on points.
* `New.IsGroupBaseChange`: base change, compatible with the group structure and the `O`-action;
  Mathlib's pullback carries both structures.
* `New.IsAbelianScheme`: smooth and proper, with surjective multiplication by every `m ≠ 0`.
  Divisibility is asked for where one usually asks for connected fibres.
* `New.Pic.atPoint`, `New.Pic.pairing`, `New.Pic.ParallelogramLaw`: for a class `c` in the Picard
  group `New.Pic` (written additively), its pull-back along a point, the pairing of two points, and
  the parallelogram law.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Pic.pull`: For p: Y → X, the homomorphism Pic X → Pic Y sending the class of a line bundle to
  the class of its pull-back.

modules.title: Pairings of line bundle classes on abelian schemes and their fpqc descent
modules.group: Abelian schemes over a base and their isogenies
modules.note:
This file studies classes of line bundles on commutative group schemes and abelian schemes. Line
bundles are cocycles (`New.LineBundle`), and `New.Pic` is written additively. For a class `c` and
points `x`, `y`, the pairing `New.Pic.pairing c x y` is the class (x + y)^*c − x^*c − y^*c + 0^*c.
The file proves rules for the pairing, a quasi-finiteness criterion, and stability of abelian
schemes under base change. It also treats the descent of identities between pairings along an fpqc
cover.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.locallyQuasiFinite_of_pull_picClass`: a map that pulls a class back to a nonzero
  multiple of an embedding class is locally quasi-finite.
* `New.Pic.ParallelogramLaw.pairing_nsmul_left`, `New.Variety.pairing_comm`,
  `New.Variety.pairing_comp`: rules for the pairing.
* `New.Variety.pull_nsmul_eq_sq_smul`: over a local ring, multiplication by `m` pulls `c` back to
  `m² c` if `c` satisfies the parallelogram law.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Pic.atPoint`: For c in Pic A and a T-point x of A, the pull-back x^*c in Pic T.
* `New.Pic.ParallelogramLaw`: (x + y)^*c + (x − y)^*c + 2·0^*c = 2(x^*c + y^*c) for all points.
* `New.IsAbelianScheme`: a commutative group scheme A over S is abelian if it is smooth and proper
  over S and multiplication by every m ≠ 0 is surjective.
* `New.LineBundle.IsProjEmbedding L s`: `L` embeds `X` in projective space over `S`: it is a linear
  system, `s` is proper, and points of one chart with the same coordinates and the same image in `S`
  are equal.

modules.title: Isogenies: factorisation of homomorphisms, finiteness and flatness
modules.group: Abelian schemes over a base and their isogenies
modules.note:
Two facts on isogenies. Over an Artinian ring, a homomorphism that kills the kernel of an isogeny
factors through it. Over a local ring, a quasi-finite surjective homomorphism of abelian schemes is
an isogeny.

* `New.Variety.exists_isAdditive_comp_eq_of_isIsogeny`: over an Artinian ring, a homomorphism that
  kills the kernel of an isogeny `f`, tested on finite local algebras, factors through `f`.
* `New.Variety.isIsogeny_of_locallyQuasiFinite`: over a local ring, a locally quasi-finite
  surjective homomorphism of abelian schemes is finite and flat.

Notions from other files:
* `New.specOver`: The spectrum of an R-algebra B, as a scheme over Spec R.
* `New.IsAbelianScheme`: A commutative group scheme that is smooth and proper over the base, and on
  which multiplication by every m ≠ 0 is surjective.
* `New.IsIsogeny`: A homomorphism that is finite, flat and surjective.
modules.literature:
Known result: Factorisation through an isogeny, and quasi-finite surjective homomorphisms of abelian
schemes are finite flat. Here an abelian scheme means a smooth and proper commutative group scheme
on which multiplication by every m ≠ 0 is surjective; the base is an Artinian ring for the first
result and a local ring for the second. Source: B. Edixhoven, G. van der Geer, B. Moonen, Abelian
Varieties (draft), ch. IV §3; The Stacks project, Section 0BF9; EGA IV and S. Bosch, W.
Lütkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Néron Models (1990) 7.3, 8.1.

modules.title: Étale coordinates at zero, infinitesimal points and unramified torsion
modules.group: Abelian schemes over a base and their isogenies
modules.note:
Let A be a commutative group scheme over S with an action of a ring O. The file studies the tangent
space of A at 0 through coordinate functions evaluated at points that vanish modulo a square-zero
ideal.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.IsSqZeroExt`, `New.IsInfinitesimal`, `New.tangentCoords`: square-zero extensions ψ, points
  that vanish modulo ker ψ, and their coordinates z(y) − z(0).
* `New.IsEtaleChart`, `New.exists_isEtaleChart`: étale coordinates; they exist on a smooth scheme.
* `New.IsLieChart`, `New.exists_isLieChart`: coordinates at 0 that are additive on infinitesimal
  points and in which O acts by matrices.
* `New.HasSignature`, `New.HasSignature.of_points`: the rank-one signature condition for ρ, b, b' on
  these matrices passes from a jointly injective family of ring maps to every map φ into a local
  ring for which φ(ρ b − ρ b') is a unit.
* `New.Variety.eq_zero_of_nsmul_eq_zero_of_comp_eq_zero`: torsion of invertible order in an abelian
  scheme over a local ring is unramified. The ideal I cutting out the locus where the section
  vanishes satisfies I ≤ I² by
  `New.IsInfinitesimal.eq_zero_of_isUnit_and_nsmul_eq_zero_of_cast_eq_zero`, so I = 0 by Nakayama's
  lemma.

Notions from other files:
* `New.IsAbelianScheme`: a commutative group scheme A over S is abelian if it is smooth and proper
  over S and multiplication by every m ≠ 0 is surjective.

modules.title: Reduction of isogeny kernels: Cartier density, the tangent line and torsion sections
modules.group: The congruence relation at split places
modules.note:
The file studies how kernels of isogenies of abelian schemes in a family `X : New.ThetaFamily D Z τ`
reduce from a valuation subring of `ℂ` to a field. The file records what goodness of the PEL data
gives at the kernel of a map to a field. It also finds the line of tangent vectors on which `𝓞 E`
acts through `x.baseHom`. From this line it gets a function that detects tangent vectors, and from
that function a parameter `t` whose powers are local equations for the torsion sections.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.cartier`: a function on a finite flat subgroup scheme (or coset) of a commutative
  group scheme that vanishes at all `K`-points is zero, for `K` an algebraically closed field of
  characteristic zero containing the base ring.
* `New.Variety.ker_factors_of_points`: over a valuation ring with fraction field `ℂ`, a closed
  condition that holds for the torsion complex points of the kernel of a finite flat homomorphism
  holds for all points of the kernel.
* `New.Variety.placeTorsion`: the points of `x.groupScheme` with values in a `k`-algebra `C` that
  are killed by the kernel of `x.baseHom`.
* `New.Variety.ker_factors_of_torsionPoint`: the torsion sections are dense in the kernel of an
  isogeny.
* `New.Variety.exists_isLieLine`: the line of tangent vectors on which `𝓞 E` acts through
  `x.baseHom`.
* `New.Variety.exists_isLocalEquation_pow_sectionCount`: at a local point `z` of the special fibre
  killed by a power of `β - b`, the power `t ^ N` of a parameter `t` is a local equation for a
  family of torsion sections, `N` of which pass through the closed point of `z`.
* `New.Variety.exists_param_pow_card_eq_zero`: the resulting parameter at a point killed by
  `ker x.baseHom`, and a nonzero torsion section that reduces to zero.

Notions from other files:
* `New.ThetaObject`: An object of the family X over a scheme T: a morphism x from T to the base of
  X; `x.groupScheme` is the pull-back of the abelian scheme along it.
* `New.ThetaObject.baseHom`: For an object x over Spec R, the ring homomorphism O_E → R induced by x
  and the structure morphism of the base of the family to Spec O_E.
* `New.AddObj`: A commutative group object.
* `New.specOver`: The spectrum of an R-algebra B, as a scheme over Spec R.
* `New.ValuativeArc`: A valuation ring O with fraction field ℂ, with its generic point Spec ℂ → Spec
  O.

modules.title: The congruence relation and the trivial action of inertia on ℓ-adic cohomology
modules.group: The congruence relation at split places
modules.note:
The Eichler–Shimura argument: a relation between Frobenius twists of points in characteristic p
gives a relation between pull-backs and Galois action on ℓ-adic cohomology.

* `New.Variety.ellAdicCohom.ellAdicPull_frobEnd`: the absolute Frobenius acts trivially on
  cohomology.
* `New.Variety.ellAdicCohom.congruence_relation`: the congruence relation
  `New.Variety.CongruenceRelation` on points gives ∑ mᵢ uᵢ^* g^(−eᵢ) = 0 on Vⁿ(Y), for a Frobenius
  element g.
* `New.Variety.ellAdicCohom.galoisAction_eq_one_of_inertia`: inertia acts trivially (the case q = 1
  of the relation).

The idea: extend classes from Ω to the valuation ring A, then restrict to the special fibre.
`New.Variety.ellAdicCohom` is X ↦ Vⁿ(X) = ℚ_ℓ ⊗ Hⁿ(X_Ω, ℤ_ℓ), with the action
`New.Variety.ellAdicCohom.galoisAction` of Γ; `New.Variety.ellAdicPull` is the pull-back along a map
of free abelian functors (`freeAb` sends a functor to its pointwise free abelian group);
`New.Variety.IsCharted` is the hypothesis on Y that stands in for smoothness: it gives smooth base
change, so that pull-back from A to Ω is bijective on the cohomology of Y.

Notions from other files:
* `New.IsFrob`: σ stabilises the valuation subring A and σx ≡ x^q modulo the maximal ideal for all x
  in A; for q = 1 this is membership in the inertia group.
* `New.Variety.mapOnTests`: For a map u: X → Y of set-valued functors on rings, its restriction to a
  map of functors on test rings.
* `New.Variety.ellAdicCoeff`: The coefficient `ℤ_ℓ`: a test ring `A` goes to the Witt vectors of the
  ring of locally constant functions `Spec A → 𝔽_ℓ`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Smooth proper reduction gives unramified ℓ-adic cohomology, and Frobenius relations
pass to it. Here the base is the valuation ring of a place. Source: Stacks project, Tags 0GKD (SGA4
XVI 2.2) and 03SN (SGA5 XV); Deligne, Formes modulaires et représentations ℓ-adiques, Sém. Bourbaki
355 (1969).

modules.title: Hecke elements on adelic torsion and reductions of Frobenius twists of Hecke neighbours
modules.group: The congruence relation at split places
modules.note:
Fix a split place `w` of the CM field `E` and a subspace `C` of `(𝓞 / w)ⁿ`, and let `q` be the order
of the residue field. This file describes how the Hecke element `New.Variety.invHeckeIsogeny w C`
acts on the torsion module `New.AdelicTorsion E n`, which is `(𝔸_f / Ô)ⁿ`. These computations are
combined with Frobenius-twisted reductions of linear maps to prove
`New.Variety.UniversalFamily.exists_ne_bot_factorsThrough_sup`. This result is the geometric step
behind the congruence relation at `w`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.exists_residue_torsion_emb`: the `w`-torsion is `(𝓞 / w)ⁿ`, compatibly with integral
  matrices.
* `New.Variety.frobeniusTwist`: the absolute Frobenius of a `k`-scheme, as a map between its two
  structures over `V`.
* `New.Variety.IsTwistedReduction`: a map between reductions is the reduction of a map `ψ` twisted
  by a Frobenius.
* `New.Variety.IsTwistedReduction.exists_comp_eq_smul`: a multiple of one twisted reduction factors
  through another.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.invHeckeIsogeny`: For a subspace U of k_wⁿ of dimension r, the product of a central
  factor, the conjugate of N(ϖ_w)^(−r) with N the norm from E to ℚ(√−d₀), and a unitary local
  factor, which is (`New.basicCosetRep` U)⁻¹ at w and 1 away from w and w̄.
* `New.basicCosetRep`: For a subspace U of k_wⁿ of dimension r, a matrix in the double coset of
  diag(ϖ 1_r, 1) in GL_n(E_w) whose reduction modulo w has kernel U.
* `New.Variety.SplitFinPlace`: The finite places w of E with w̄ ≠ w, that is, those split over the
  maximal real subfield.
* `New.Variety.IsSafe`: The place u of ℚ(√−d₀) below w contains some (1 + √−d₀)/2 − b coprime to its
  conjugate (so u is split), and the level 𝔑 lies neither in w nor in a place above ū.
modules.literature:
Known result: Pointwise step of the Eichler–Shimura congruence relation for GU(1,n−1) at a split
place. Only the geometric step is treated here, and it uses no ordinary locus. At each geometric
point of the special fibre, the Frobenius-twisted Hecke neighbour of a subspace depends only on its
sum with one fixed non-zero subspace. Source: Wedhorn, Congruence relations on some Shimura
varieties, J. reine angew. Math. 524 (2000) 43–71; the method follows Katz–Mazur 1985 ch. 13 and
Harris–Taylor 2001 III.4.

modules.title: Counting w-torsion points bounds a space of natural semilinear functions by n − 1
modules.group: First-order deformations and the tangent space bound
modules.note:
`x` is a `k`-point of a family of abelian schemes with `𝓞 E`-action (`New.ThetaObject`).
`x.groupScheme` is its abelian variety, `x.baseHom : 𝓞 E → k` is the structure map and `w` its
kernel. A morphism `specOver k C ⟶ x.groupScheme` is a `C`-point, and `placeTorsion x C` is the
`𝓞 E`-module of the `C`-points killed by `w`; `placeTorsionMap ψ` carries such points along
`ψ : C → C'`, composing with `specOver.map ψ`. The main result is
`New.Variety.finrank_le_of_placeTorsion`; there `n = Fintype.card D.Index`.

modules.title: Drinfeld lifting over k[ε] and a bound on the tangent space of the moduli scheme
modules.group: First-order deformations and the tangent space bound
modules.note:
In the first two sections, `x` and `x'` are first-order deformations over `k[ε]` of one object `x₀`
over a field `k`, in a family `New.ThetaFamily` of abelian schemes. In the third section, `x` is a
first-order deformation of `x₀` over `k ⊕ M*`. `New.Variety.sqZeroReduction k k` is
`Spec k ⟶ Spec k[ε]`, and `New.ThetaObject.IsPullbackAlong b x₀ x` exhibits `x₀` as the pull-back of
`x` along `b`. In the second section, `k` is algebraically closed of prime characteristic. There,
`f : x.groupScheme ⟶ x'.groupScheme` is a homomorphism that reduces to multiplication by `a` on
`x₀.groupScheme`. If `a ≠ 0`, a homomorphism `F` that reduces to `c * a` and kills the kernel of `f`
yields a homomorphism out of `x'.groupScheme` that reduces to `c`. These tools give the tangent
bound for deformations without constant directions.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.AgreeModEps`: points of `x.groupScheme` and `x'.groupScheme` with the same reduction
  modulo `ε`. The points that agree with `0` are those that vanish modulo `ε`.
  `New.Variety.AgreeModEps.ringChar_smul_and_smul_eq_zero` gives elements that kill them.
* `New.Variety.drinfeld_lift`: if `c` kills the points of `x'.groupScheme` that vanish modulo `ε`,
  then multiplication by `c` on `x₀.groupScheme` lifts to a homomorphism
  `x.groupScheme ⟶ x'.groupScheme`.
* `New.Variety.isLinear_and_pairing_eq_of_reduction`: such an `f` is linear, and `a` kills its
  kernel modulo `ε`. The lemma also describes its effect on the pairing.
* `New.Variety.finrank_tangent_le_card_index_sub_one`: under the hypotheses stated in its docstring,
  if a first-order deformation `x` over `k ⊕ M*` of `x₀` has no constant direction in `M`, then
  `finrank k M ≤ Fintype.card D.Index - 1`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.ThetaObject`: An object of the family X over a scheme T: a morphism from T to the base of X.
* `New.ThetaObject.groupScheme`: The group scheme with O_E-action of an object x over S: the
  pull-back of the abelian scheme of the family along x : S → base.
* `New.Pic.pairing`: For c in Pic A and T-points x, y of A, the class ⟨x,
  y⟩ = (x + y)^*c − x^*c − y^*c + 0^*c in Pic T (`New.Pic.atPoint` is x ↦ x^*c).
* `New.IsGroupBaseChange.pointEquiv`: For an O-compatible base change p : A' → A and an S'-scheme T,
  the O-linear bijection x ↦ p∘x from T-points of A' over S' to T-points of A over S.
modules.literature:
Known result: Deformations of the PEL object have at most n - 1 parameters, where n is the size of
the index set `D.Index`. Only the upper bound for first-order deformations is proved here, at every
good place, working on the finite group scheme of w-torsion with Drinfeld's lifting lemma and
without p-divisible groups or crystals. Source: N. Katz, Serre–Tate local moduli, LNM 868 (1981), §1
(Drinfeld's lemma); J. Lubin, J. Tate, Formal moduli for one-parameter formal Lie groups, Bull. SMF
94 (1966); M. Harris, R. Taylor, The Geometry and Cohomology of Some Simple Shimura Varieties
(2001), III.4.1.

modules.title: Sizes of theta functions at torsion points: products, bounds and shift bounds
modules.group: Good reduction of theta tori
modules.note:
Theta functions (`New.RealComplexForm.thetaSpace`) on a complex torus `V / L`, measured at the
torsion points by a valuation `v` on `ℂ`. The degree is a form `B` (a `LatticeForm L`: it has
complex values B x y, and degrees are added and scaled by reals) with Appell–Humbert data
`New.IsAppellHumbert` and Riemann form `New.RealComplexForm.riemannForm`;
`New.RealComplexForm.thetaShift` is translation with the exponential factor that keeps the degree.
The size `New.ThetaTori.LatticeForm.sizeAt` of `f` at a torsion point `x` is
`v (exp (-B x x / 2) * f x)`, and `New.ThetaTori.LatticeForm.sizes` is the set of all sizes of
degree `B`, over all multipliers χ of finite order with `New.ThetaTori.IsAmpleType`. Roots of unity
have valuation `1`, so sizes are periodic and do not see these multipliers.

* `New.ThetaTori.mul_shift_mem_sizes`: products of sizes with torsion translates of sizes are sizes.
* `New.ThetaTori.bddAbove_of_mem_sizes`, `New.ThetaTori.IsAmpleType.thetaNorm_pos`: sizes are
  bounded, and the sup norm of `f ≠ 0` is positive.
* `New.ThetaTori.eq_zero_of_torsionPoints`: a holomorphic function that vanishes at all torsion
  points is zero.
* `New.ThetaTori.LatticeForm.HasShiftBound`: the bound `φ ^ 2 ≤ C * ⨆ x, φ x * φ (x + w)`. It passes
  from `B` to `B'` when the Riemann form of `B - B'` is positive
  (`New.ThetaTori.LatticeForm.HasShiftBound.of_isPosRiemann_sub`), and with `C = 1` it compares
  products of translates (`New.ThetaTori.mul_le_iSup_of_hasShiftBound`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.IsPosRiemann`: The Riemann form E of B is positive: E(u, iu) > 0 for every u ≠ 0.
* `New.RealComplexForm.dualLattice`: The dual of L for the Riemann form E of B: the v in V with E(v,
  l) an integer for all l in L.

modules.title: Hermitian tori with multiplications, Gauss sums and unfolding of the Poincaré kernel
modules.group: Good reduction of theta tori
modules.note:
Let `V / L` be a complex torus with multiplications `F` by a ring `R` with involution and a
polarising hermitian form `B`. The hypothesis `New.ThetaTori.IsHermitianAction` gives the
compatibilities between these data.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.ThetaTori.IsHermitianAction`: `B` is positive hermitian, its Riemann form is integral on `L`,
  `F (star a)` is adjoint to `F a`, and `star β = 1 - β`.
* `New.ThetaTori.IsHermitianAction.isAppellHumbert`: the canonical multiplier
  `New.ThetaTori.IsHermitianAction.multiplier` of `F β` gives Appell–Humbert data.
* `New.ThetaTori.IsHermitianAction.MulKernel`, `New.ThetaTori.IsHermitianAction.card_mulKernel`: the
  kernel `a⁻¹ L / L` of `a ≠ 0` on the torus has order `|det (F a)|²`.
* `New.ThetaTori.IsHermitianAction.normShift_sum_eq_char_smul`: averaging normalised translates over
  this kernel against a character gives an eigenvector.
* `New.ThetaTori.IsHermitianAction.sum_conj_pow_four_eq_sum_pow_four`: a quadratic Gauss sum over
  `κ⁻¹ L / L` has a real fourth power.
* `New.ThetaTori.IsHermitianAction.isSelfAdjoint_quotMean_pow`: the mean of `x ↦ K(c̄ x, c x)` times
  `conj (det c̄)` has a real fourth power; unfolding writes the mean as a Gauss sum times a Gaussian
  integral.

Notions from other files:
* `New.RealComplexForm.riemannForm`: The Riemann form of B: the alternating real form
  E(u, v) = Im(B(u,v) − B(v,u))/(2π).
* `New.ThetaTori.normalizedShift`: The twisted translation `New.RealComplexForm.thetaShift`,
  f ↦ (z ↦ exp(−B(x, z) − B(x, x)/2) f(z + x)), divided by the canonical multiplier at x.
* `New.IsAppellHumbert`: Appell–Humbert data: Re B is symmetric, and on L one has |χ| = 1 and
  χ(l + m) = χ(l)χ(m)·exp(πi E(m, l)), E the Riemann form of B.
* `New.IsAppellHumbert.poincareSeries`:
  K(x, y) = ∑_{l ∈ L} exp(B(x, y − x + l) − B(l,y) − B(l,l)/2)/χ(l), the sum of the terms
  `New.IsAppellHumbert.poincareTerm`.

modules.title: Good reduction of theta tori from shift bounds on kernels of multiplications
modules.group: Good reduction of theta tori
modules.note:
The file gives a criterion for the main condition of good reduction of a torus `V / L` with
multiplications `New.ThetaTori.IsHermitianAction`. The condition
(`New.ThetaTori.HasMultiplicativeNorm`) is that the sup norm of sizes of theta functions is
multiplicative at the valuation `v`. The tool is a shift bound: `A.HasShiftBound v w C` (`w` has
the constant `C` in degree `A`) says `φ y ^ 2 ≤ C * ⨆ x, φ x * φ (x + w)` for all sizes `φ` of theta
functions of degree `A` and all torsion points `y`. Constants are obtained on the kernels of
multiplications `c` and descend along `c`, which gives multiplicativity.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.ThetaTori.IsHermitianAction.hasShiftBound_one_of_ker`: under arithmetic conditions on `c`,
  its kernel has the constant `1`.
* `New.ThetaTori.IsHermitianAction.hasShiftBound_of_torsionAction`,
  `New.ThetaTori.IsHermitianAction.eventually_hasShiftBound`: a constant descends along `c`; some
  constant exists.
* `New.ThetaTori.IsHermitianAction.hasMultiplicativeNorm_of_frequently_hasShiftBound`: if such `c`
  have arbitrarily small inverses, `New.ThetaTori.HasMultiplicativeNorm` holds.
* `New.ThetaTori.hasMultiplicativeNorm_of_expanding`: the multiplicative norm from arithmetic
  conditions on `R`, `B` and `p`.
* `New.ThetaTori.ThetaTorus.hasGoodReduction_and_val_card_eq_one`: let `v` be a valuation on `ℂ`
  whose valuation ring receives `𝓞 E` compatibly with `Φ v₀`, over a prime that is good for `D`.
  Then a theta torus has good reduction for `v`, and the order of `D.dualTorsion` is a unit.

Notions from other files:
* `New.ThetaTori.IsHermitianAction.multiplier`: The canonical multiplier x ↦ exp(πi E(βx, x)) of the
  hermitian data, where E is the Riemann form of B.
* `New.ThetaTori.HasGoodReduction`: a polarisation whose dual lattice is mapped into the lattice by
  a `v`-unit, a level `r > 1` that is a `v`-unit, and a multiplicative sup norm of theta functions
  on the torsion points.
modules.literature:
Known result: Good reduction of unitary PEL abelian varieties, in analytic form without toric
degeneration. Suppose a torus with polarisation prime to p has non-unit multipliers that expand
arbitrarily, divide a power of p and are prime to their conjugates, and whose conjugates have unit
determinant on the Lie algebra. Then the supremum of a valuation of theta values at torsion points
is multiplicative. Source: K.-W. Lan, Elevators for degenerations of PEL structures, Math. Res.
Lett. 18 (2011); R. Kottwitz, Points on some Shimura varieties over finite fields, J. Amer. Math.
Soc. 5 (1992), §5 (division algebra case); for the CM case B. Conrad, Semistable reduction for
abelian varieties (notes), Prop. 6.3, after Serre and Tate, Ann. of Math. 88 (1968).

modules.title: Hecke elements in group rings, marked triples, local terms and neat levels
modules.group: Hecke operators on a tower of Kuga–Sato varieties
modules.note:
Hecke operators for a group `G` with a subgroup `K` are realised inside the group ring `k[G]`, so
they act on every representation of `G` without convolution. With this, the file sets up the data
for counting fixed points of Hecke correspondences for a CM field `E` over K₀ = ℚ(√-d₀). A rigidity
result for frames then shows that the objects counted have no automorphisms at deep level: levels
inside a large place are neat.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.fixedToEigen`: the elements that send `K`-fixed vectors to eigenvectors of a
  subgroup, in every representation.
* `New.Variety.MarkedTriple`, `New.Variety.countTerm`: triples (coset, rational matrix, mark) and
  the term that an orbit of triples contributes; `New.Variety.IsRegularHecke`: only separable
  matrices contribute.
* `New.Variety.IsSafe`, `New.Variety.invHeckeIsogeny`, `New.Variety.heckeSum`: the safe split places
  and the Hecke elements that appear in the congruence relation.
* `New.Variety.localTerm`: the local term of a fixed point, a polynomial whose coefficients are
  built from the roots of the characteristic polynomial.
* `New.Variety.IsSignedFrameFor.similitude_and_root_norm`: an automorphism scales the form, and its
  eigenvalues have equal moduli.
* `New.Variety.IsSignedFrameFor.eq_one_of_congr_large_norm`: if such an automorphism is congruent to
  `1` modulo an ideal of large norm, it is `1`.
* `New.Variety.eventually_isNeat`: hence levels inside a large place are neat.

Notions from other files:
* `New.levelSpace`: For a representation π of G, a subgroup K and a character χ of K, the submodule
  of vectors v with π(k)v = χ(k)v for all k in K; for χ = 1, the K-fixed vectors.
* `New.ofSplitPlace`: For a split place w, the homomorphism sending g in GL_n(E_w) to the unitary
  finite adelic matrix with component g at w and 1 off w, w̄.
* `New.Variety.GU`: The unitary similitudes: the frames of the scalar forms `c • 1`, `c > 0`
  rational. `New.Variety.GUPlus`: those whose inverse has integral entries.
* `New.Gf`: The finite adelic unitary group G_f: matrices g in GL_n(𝔸_f) with gᴴg = 1;
  `New.stdLevel` is its subgroup of integral points, `New.stdSpace E n` the definite space with form
  `1`.
* `New.basicCosetRep U`: for a subspace U of k_wⁿ of dimension r (k_w the residue field at w), a
  chosen g in GL_n(E_w) with g and ϖg⁻¹ integral, det g of valuation r, and U the kernel of the
  reduction of g.
* `New.levelOf w H`: the elements of `New.stdLevel` whose reductions modulo the places `w i` lie in
  `H`; `New.classAut Γ K g`: the stabiliser Γ ∩ gKg⁻¹ of the coset gK.

modules.title: Properties of a Kuga–Sato tower, Hecke operators at split places, torsion counts and levels
modules.group: Hecke operators on a tower of Kuga–Sato varieties
modules.note:
The structure `New.Variety.Model` collects the geometry of a tower of Kuga–Sato varieties that the
point count uses. K(𝔑) denotes the principal level `New.Variety.levelGU n 𝔑`. τ_{w,j} denotes the
Hecke element `New.Variety.heckeSum` at a safe split place w of E. The file shows that these
elements lie in the Hecke algebra of K(𝔑). It counts the `I`-torsion of the adelic module
`New.AdelicTorsion E n`: it has N(I) ^ card n elements, where N(I) is the norm of the ideal I. It
proves finiteness statements for multiplication by integers on the abelian schemes of a family
`X : New.ThetaFamily D Z τ`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.Model`: the tower of varieties with its properties.
* `New.Variety.asAlgebraHom_heckeSum`: τ_{w,j} acts on K(𝔑)-fixed vectors as a central element times
  the j-th Hecke operator of GL_n(E_w); `New.Variety.tauHecke` is τ_{w,j} in the Hecke algebra.
* `New.Variety.Model.exists_isHeckeAction`: the commuting operators on F(Z), for the base Z of a
  model and a functor F with descent.
* `New.card_torsionBySet_adelicTorsion`: for `I ≠ 0` the `I`-torsion of `New.AdelicTorsion E n` has
  `N(I) ^ card n` elements.
* `New.Variety.exists_level_conj_mem`: a principal level deep enough for finitely many isogenies.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.SplitFinPlace`: The finite places w of E with w̄ ≠ w, that is, those split over the
  maximal real subfield.
* `New.Variety.levelGU`: the principal level K(𝔑), the similitudes in `GL_n(Ô E)` that are congruent
  to `1` modulo `𝔑`.
* `New.Variety.conjAtSplit w g`: for a split place w, the adelic matrix that is g⁻ᵀ at w, the
  conjugate of g at w̄, and 1 elsewhere.
* `New.Variety.heckeSum n k w j`: the Hecke element τ_{w,j}, the sum of
  `New.Variety.invHeckeIsogeny w U` over the subspaces U of dimension j.
* `New.Variety.IsSafe`: Safe places w of E: the place u of ℚ(√−d₀) below w satisfies
  `New.GaloisRep.IsSplitPrimeToDisc`, and 𝔑 lies neither in w nor in any place above ū.
modules.literature:
Known result: Hecke algebra of a pair acting by correspondences on the base of a tower. Here only a
semigroup acts, and only far enough up the tower, and the algebra is a subalgebra of the group ring.
The cohomology theory may be any functor to modules for which the base is the invariants of each
cover. Source: Shimura, Introduction to the arithmetic theory of automorphic functions, 1971, ch. 3
and 7–8.

See also `Lib.Shimura.IntegralModel.TowerExistence`, `Lib.Shimura.Uniformisation.AppellHumbert` and
`Lib.Shimura.AbelianScheme.IsogenyFlatness`.

modules.title: Existence of PEL data at levels good at all safe places, with the form ξ and a Lagrangian
modules.group: Construction of the integral model of the moduli tower
modules.note:
PEL data (`New.PEL`) are the arithmetic input of the moduli problem; this file constructs them.

* `New.Variety.exists_lagrangian`: an isotropic set lies in a self-annihilating subgroup.
* `New.Variety.IsSafeGoodPEL`: PEL data of given rank, level and `β`, good at all safe places.
* `New.Variety.exists_pel`: PEL data of any nonzero rank at every nonzero level divisible by some
  `N` that lies in none of the places of a given finite set `B`, good at all safe places.

Conventions: `CMBase E` is a CM type `Φ` together with a base place `v₀`; `Φ v` is the embedding the
CM type picks at `v`, `ψf` the standard character of the finite adeles, `xiForm ξ x y = ξ yᴴ x`,
`Ô E` the integral finite adeles, and `torsionClass` the quotient map onto
`AdelicTorsion E (Fin n)`, whose kernel is the vectors with entries in `Ô E`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.HasPrimitiveRoot5040`: `E` contains a primitive root of unity of order `7! = 5040`.
* `New.Variety.IsSafe 𝔑 w` (for `ℚ(√−d)` in `E`): the place u of ℚ(√−d) below w contains some
  (1 + √−d)/2 − b, b ∈ ℤ, that is coprime to its conjugate, and 𝔑 lies neither in w nor in any place
  above ū.

modules.title: The universal family: models along arcs, rigid fibres and points of linear data
modules.group: Construction of the integral model of the moduli tower
modules.note:
This file studies the universal abelian scheme 𝒜 → S of PEL data D and describes its complex points
by linear algebra. Over an arc `O` (`New.ValuativeArc`, a valuation ring with fraction field `ℂ`), a
description of the generic fibre as a complex torus (`New.ThetaObject.TorusModel`) is also a
description of the object over `O`. The geometric fibres of such a modelled object are rigid
(`New.ThetaObject.HasSpanningCoords`): on each of their pull-backs to a noetherian local ring `B`,
global functions come from the base (`New.HasConstFunctions`), and the coordinates span the sections
of the line bundle `N` of the object over `B`. A linear datum a = (x, ℓ, P)
(`New.Variety.ModuliPoint`) consists of an adelic frame x, a reflection ℓ of ℂⁿ (1 on a line, −1 on
a complement), and vectors P_i.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.UniversalFamily`: the universal object, with the standing hypotheses.
* `New.ThetaFamily.IsPointOf`, `New.Variety.UniversalFamily.datumPoint`: the point of a fibre power
  of 𝒜 given by a fibre modelled on a, its non-zero 𝔪-torsion points and the images of the P_i.
* `New.ThetaFamily.IsPointOf.eq_iff`, `New.Variety.UniversalFamily.datumPoint_eq_iff`: two such
  points are equal exactly when the data are isomorphic (`New.Variety.ModuliPoint.IsLevelIso`) at
  level K(𝔑) ∩ K(𝔪), where K is the principal level `New.Variety.levelGU` and 𝔑 the level of D. Here
  a ≅ b via z in GL_n(E) means: b.x⁻¹ z a.x lies in the level group, z conjugates a's reflection to
  b's, and z P_i − b.P_i lies in the lattice of b.x.
* `New.Variety.UniversalFamily.GraphClosure`: the closure of the graph of finitely many translations
  a ↦ a·(g_j, 1).
* `New.Variety.UniversalFamily.smooth_and_isDenseFamily_and_exists_comp_eq_act`: at level 1 the
  fibre power is smooth over R, and the points of linear data are dense in it.

Notions from other files:
* `New.ThetaObject`: an object of the family X over a scheme T: a morphism from T to the base of X;
  `x.IsPullbackAlong f y` means x = f ≫ y, the pull-back of y along f.
* `New.Variety.ModuliPoint.act`: a·(g, α) = (x g, ℓ, α_i P_i) for a = (x, ℓ, P), an adelic
  similitude g and integers α_i of E.
* `New.ThetaObject.TorusModel.π`: for a model m, the map from (E ⊗ ℝ)ⁿ to the sections of the
  object; `m.fullStructure.torsionPoint` labels the torsion sections by `New.AdelicTorsion`.
* `New.Variety.NonzeroTorsion`: for a non-zero element 𝔪 of O_E, the set of non-zero elements of
  (𝔸_f / Ô)ⁿ ≅ (E / O_E)ⁿ killed by 𝔪.
modules.literature:
Known result: the sections of an ample line bundle on an abelian variety are spanned by theta
functions. Here it is stated for the coordinates of an object with a torus model, on the pull-backs
of its geometric fibres to noetherian local rings (`hasSpanningCoords_of_specMap_comp_eq`). Spanning
of the sections is proved by reduction from the complex numbers rather than by Riemann–Roch, and the
only consequence drawn is that a map of such objects respecting the pairing and the level points
lies over the family, which gives the criterion for equal points (`IsPointOf.eq_iff`). Source: D.
Mumford, On the equations defining abelian varieties I, Invent. Math. 1 (1966), §§1–2; S. W. Shin,
Abelian varieties and Weil representations, Algebra Number Theory 6 (2012), Prop. 2.12 (over a
base); M. Bolognesi, A. Massarenti, Comment. Math. Helv. 91 (2016), Lemma 4.1 (odd type).

See also `Lib.Shimura.ArcExtension` and `Lib.Shimura.IntegralModel.TowerExistence`.

modules.title: Balls immerse; holomorphy, arcs and complex points of the covers
modules.group: Construction of the integral model of the moduli tower
modules.note:
This file gives a local and global description of the covers
`New.Variety.UniversalFamily.GraphClosure`. These are reduced closures `C.scheme` of the complex
points `C.point a`. Here `a = (x, ℓ, P)` (`New.Variety.ModuliPoint`) is an adelic frame, a
reflection (1 on a line, −1 on a complement) and marked vectors.

* `New.Variety.AnalyticFamily.isHolomorphicImmersionAt_of_holomorphicAt`: let the objects `x b'`
  have models of the tori of an analytic family. Let `b` be in its domain. Suppose the uniformised
  points are holomorphic at `(b, z)` for every `z`. Then `x` is a holomorphic immersion at `b`.
* `New.Variety.ModuliPoint.exists_finite_analyticFamily_isLevelIso`: at each nonzero level, finitely
  many analytic families reach every point up to isomorphism.
* `New.Variety.UniversalFamily.isHolomorphicImmersionAt_datumPoint`,
  `New.Variety.UniversalFamily.GraphClosure.holomorphicAt_point`: the points of an analytic family
  depend holomorphically, and immersively, on the parameter.
* `New.Variety.UniversalFamily.GraphClosure.exists_arc`,
  `New.Variety.UniversalFamily.GraphClosure.exists_arc_centre_eq`: every point of `C.scheme`, and
  every complex point, is the centre of an arc of objects.
* `New.Variety.UniversalFamily.GraphClosure.point_surjective`: suppose some map `c` sends each
  `C.point a` to `U.datumPoint 1 a`. Then every complex point of `C.scheme` is some `C.point a`.

`New.HolomorphicAt φ w` says that regular functions pull back along `φ` to functions analytic at
`w`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.AnalyticFamily`: tori with a fixed frame over a domain `f.domain` in ℂⁿ⁻¹, with
  period maps `Q_b` analytic in `b`; the derivative of `Q` along `v` is ℂ-linear for the complex
  structure given by `Q_b` only if `v = 0` (`eq_zero_of_linear`).
* `New.Variety.ModuliPoint.act`: `a.act g α = (x g, ℓ, α i • P i)` for `a = (x, ℓ, P)`.
* `New.Variety.UniversalFamily.datumPoint`: for `a = (x, ℓ, P)`, a chosen complex point over `R` of
  the fibre power of the family: an object modelled on `(x, ℓ)`, with its non-zero `𝔪`-torsion
  points and the points `P`.

modules.title: Existence of the model: the tower of Kuga–Sato covers with its congruence relation
modules.group: Construction of the integral model of the moduli tower
modules.note:
The end of the construction of the moduli tower. It goes from a universal family of PEL type
(`New.Variety.UniversalFamily`) to the structure `New.Variety.Model`, which is all that the point
counts use.

* `New.Variety.exists_model`: the model exists.
* `New.Variety.UniversalFamily.GraphClosure.congruenceRelation`,
  `New.Variety.UniversalFamily.GraphClosure.isTangentPoly_localTerm_of_translate`: the congruence
  relation and the tangent map at a fixed point, for the legs of a cover.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.UniversalFamily`: a universal family of PEL type over `R`: a base scheme with an
  abelian scheme over it and its standing hypotheses. `New.Variety.UniversalFamily.GraphClosure` is
  the reduced closure of the graph of finitely many translations `a ↦ a·(g_j, 1)` of complex points;
  `C.proj j` projects it to the factor `j`, sending `C.point a` to `U.datumPoint 𝔪 (a.act g)`, the
  complex point of level `𝔪`, when `γ j = (𝔪, g)`.
* `New.Variety.Model`: the tower of Kuga–Sato varieties over `R`, given by a list of properties.
* `New.Variety.Cancels`: The integers `m i` add up to zero on every fibre of `v`, that is,
  `∑ m i • [v i] = 0` in the free abelian group on `V`.
* `New.Variety.IsSafe`: Safe places w of E: the place u of ℚ(√−d₀) below w satisfies
  `New.GaloisRep.IsSplitPrimeToDisc`, and 𝔑 lies neither in w nor in any place above ū.
* `New.Variety.IsNeat`: The level 𝔑 is neat: 𝔑 ≠ 0 and, whenever `x` is a signed frame with `ℓ` for
  some form (`New.Variety.IsSignedFrame`), every y in GL_n(E) with x⁻¹yx in `levelGU n 𝔑` (the
  subgroup of level 𝔑 of GL_n(𝔸f E), inside `GUPlus E n`, whose elements translate moduli points by
  `a.act`) that fixes ℓ under `New.Variety.ratConj` equals 1.
modules.literature:
Known result: Integral Kuga–Sato models for GU(1,n−1) with level covers and the congruence relation.
Here the smooth proper base is a closure of theta values with no moduli property. The covers are
reduced projective closures of tuples of isogenous points. The model asks for smoothness of the base
only, and of the covers that they are Galois on points in characteristic zero. The congruence
relation at good split places is part of the statement.
Source: Harris, Taylor, The geometry and cohomology of some simple Shimura varieties, 2001, III.4;
Kottwitz, Points on some Shimura varieties over finite fields, JAMS 5 (1992), §5.

modules.title: Flat families of ideals cut out by points and the flat closure of theta points
modules.group: Moduli of abelian schemes embedded by theta coordinates
modules.note:
An ideal of polynomials is cut out by points in the chart `c` if it contains `X c - 1`, the forms of
degree `r ^ j` have prescribed ranks modulo the ideal, and its forms of degree `r ^ j` with `j ≤ i`
are those that vanish at given points. When the points are the images of the same `A`-valued points,
such ideals fit into a flat family over `A`, and a degree bound for monomial ideals shows that
finitely many degrees suffice.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.ThetaNull.IsCutDegree`, `New.Variety.ThetaNull.eventually_isCutDegree`: for every
  large enough `d`, a monomial ideal with at most `σ i` standard monomials of degree `r ^ i` for all
  `i ≤ d` has at most `σ i` of them in every degree `r ^ i`.
* `New.Variety.ThetaNull.eq_map_and_flat_of_isCutOut`: let `I₀` and the `I n` be cut out by the
  images of the same `A`-valued points along a local map `φ` and jointly injective maps `ψ n` to one
  field `K`, with `r > 1` and `i` such a bound. Let `T` be the polynomials over `A` that map into
  every `I n`. Then `I₀` is the reduction of `T`, and the quotient by `T` is flat.
* `New.Variety.ThetaNull.IsCutOutAt`: at a field-valued point `t` of `S`, the vanishing ideals of a
  set `Z` in the affine charts are cut out (`New.Variety.ThetaNull.IsCutOut`) by the values at `t`
  of given maps `P a` from `S` to projective space.
* `New.Variety.ThetaNull.exists_isFlatClosure`: for points `θ n z` of projective space over complex
  points `η n` of a reduced `S`, cut out (`New.Variety.ThetaNull.IsCutOutAt`) at each `η n` by
  linear systems `P`, with `r > 1` and `i` a degree bound (`New.Variety.ThetaNull.IsCutDegree`),
  where every point of `S` specialises to a geometric point at which some set is cut out, the
  reduced closure of the points over a finite dense set of the `η n` is flat over `S`, and every
  point of `S` specialises to a geometric point with reduced fibre.

Notions from other files:
* `AddSemigroupIdeal (J →₀ ℕ)` (Mathlib): a set of exponents that is closed under adding any
  exponent, that is, a monomial ideal.
* `New.LineBundle` with `New.LineBundle.IsLinearSystem`: a map from a scheme to projective space,
  given by charts and the ratios of coordinates on them.
* `New.IsDenseFamily`: a family of complex points of a scheme whose images are dense.
* `New.Variety.AllSpecializeTo`: every point of a scheme S specialises to the image of some point
  over an algebraically closed field that satisfies a property Q of field-valued points.

modules.title: PEL data, the adelic Riemann form and theta coordinates of polarised period maps
modules.group: Moduli of abelian schemes embedded by theta coordinates
modules.note:
Let `E` be a CM field with ring of integers `𝓞 E`. The file sets up the PEL data for the moduli
problem of abelian schemes with an action of `𝓞 E`. It studies polarised period maps
`x : New.ThetaTori.PeriodMap` for such data `D`. With `T = D.dualTorsion` the kernel of the
polarisation, of odd order, and `L = D.lagrangian ≤ T` Lagrangian, the file constructs lattices over
groups of torsion classes and canonical theta coordinates `θ_t` for `t ∈ T`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.PEL`: the data (rank, polarization type, level, theta structure) and their numerical
  conditions. `New.PEL.levelTorsion` is the torsion of the level.
* `New.PEL.HasClassLaws`: the laws required of the class of the embedding line bundle.
* `New.ThetaTori.PeriodMap`: a period map onto a complex vector space, with a polarisation whose
  Riemann form pulls back to `New.Variety.polarisationForm`.
* `New.Variety.fourierChar_polarisationForm`: if `gᴴ β g = a · 1`, its exponential is a value of
  `New.ψf` in the coordinates of `g`.
* `New.ThetaTori.PeriodMap.latticeOver`: the lattice in `V` over a group `S` of torsion classes.
  `New.ThetaTori.PeriodMap.periodLattice` is the lattice for `S = 0`, and its dual for the Riemann
  form is the lattice over `T` (`New.ThetaTori.PeriodMap.dualLattice_periodLattice`).
* `New.ThetaTori.PeriodMap.thetaCoord`: for `t ∈ T`, the normalised translate `θ_t` by a lift of `t`
  of the theta function `New.ThetaTori.PeriodMap.lagrangianTheta` for the
  lattice over `L`. That theta function is unique up to a scalar.
* `New.ThetaTori.PeriodMap.formSpan_eq_normBall`,
  `New.ThetaTori.PeriodMap.thetaCoord_vector_ne_zero`: at a valuation of good reduction, the forms
  of degree `r^j` in the `θ_t` fill a ball of theta functions. The `θ_t` have no common zero.

Notions from other files:
* `New.ψf`: the standard additive character of the finite adeles: ψ_f(x) = exp(2πi Tr_{E/ℚ}(a)) for
  any a in E with x − a integral.
* `New.Variety.toRealVectors`: the additive map E^n → (∏_v C)^n applying the CM-type embedding
  x ↦ (Φ_v(x))_v to each coordinate.
* `New.RealComplexForm.thetaSpace`: the entire functions f on V with
  f(z + l) = χ(l)·exp(B(l,z) + B(l,l)/2)·f(z) for l in L.
* `New.RealComplexForm.thetaShift`, `New.ThetaTori.normalizedShift`: the twisted translation
  f ↦ exp(−B(a,z) − B(a,a)/2)·f(z + a), and the same divided by the multiplier at a.
* `New.AdelicTorsion`, `New.Variety.frameTorsionClass`: the torsion O_E-module (𝔸_f / Ô)ⁿ of
  n-tuples of finite adeles of E modulo integral ones (an adelic model of (E / O_E)ⁿ), and the
  O_E-linear map sending y in Eⁿ to the class of the adelic vector g⁻¹y in it.

modules.title: Theta objects of PEL moduli problems, their pull-backs, and rigidity over local rings
modules.group: Moduli of abelian schemes embedded by theta coordinates
modules.note:
The moduli problem for a PEL datum `D : New.PEL E` is studied through one family `New.ThetaFamily`.
An object is rigid if it satisfies a constancy and spanning condition over Noetherian local rings.
Over a local Noetherian ring, rigidity yields a criterion for points in the kernel of the
polarisation to vanish. It also yields the identification of objects related by compatible
homomorphisms.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.ThetaFamily`: an abelian scheme with `𝓞 E`-action, theta coordinates and level points.
* `New.ThetaObject`: a point of the base; its abelian scheme, bundle and level points are
  pull-backs.
* `New.ThetaObject.FullLevelStructure`, `New.ThetaObject.FullLevelStructure.exists_pullback`:
  trivialisations of all torsion, and their pull-back along a local homomorphism to `ℂ`.
* `New.ThetaObject.HasSpanningCoords`: constant functions and spanning coordinates on every
  pull-back to a Noetherian local ring; such an object is called rigid.
* `New.ThetaObject.HasSpanningCoords.eq_zero_of_pairing_eq_zero`: a criterion, in characteristic
  `l`, for a point in the kernel of the polarisation to be zero.
* `New.ThetaObject.HasSpanningCoords.eq_and_comp_toFamily_eq_of_hom`: for two objects with the same
  map `𝓞 E → B`, a homomorphism that respects the action, the pairing and the level points
  identifies them.

Notions from other files:
* `New.PEL.levelTorsion`: the level module: the O_E-submodule of (𝔸_f / Ô)^rank of elements killed
  by the level 𝔑.
* `New.Pic.pairing`: for c in Pic A and T-points x, y of A, the class
  ⟨x, y⟩ = (x + y)^*c − x^*c − y^*c + 0^*c in Pic T.
* `New.Variety.IsSectionLift`: a map H⁰(L) → H⁰(L') that is pull-back along f followed by some
  isomorphism f^*L ≅ L'; `New.Variety.IsTranslationLift` is the case of a translation, L' = L.

modules.title: Linear systems and theta families from dense complex points carrying theta tori
modules.group: Moduli of abelian schemes embedded by theta coordinates
modules.note:
This file builds objects from their values at a dense family of complex points. A linear system is a
line bundle whose transition functions are the ratios `s j / s i`, that is, a map to projective
space. `New.Variety.ThetaNull.exists_isLinearSystem` extends coordinates given at a dense family `ξ`
of complex points of a reduced scheme (`New.IsSeparatingFamily`) to a linear system. It needs a
linear system `M` with homogeneous coordinates `m a` at each `ξ a`. It also needs each of `w`, `m`
to be locally a regular function times sums of the other. The result has the Picard class of `M`.
The second part builds a family of theta-embedded abelian schemes `New.ThetaFamily D` over a base
`S` from complex points `η k` of `S` that carry theta tori `x k`. The scheme `A` is the closure of
the theta points. The group law, the action and all identities extend from these points by density,
using Riemann's relation for theta functions.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_isAbelianScheme`: group and module axioms pass from dense families of vector spaces to
  `A`.
* `New.Variety.exists_maps_of_riemann_relation`: the extension step along Riemann's relation.
* `New.Variety.exists_add_and_intAction`: the addition and the action of `𝓞 E` extend to `A`.
* `New.Variety.exists_isThetaStructure`: the theta law on base changes to local rings.
* `New.Variety.exists_thetaFamily_of_points`: the family exists, modelled on `x i` at each `η i`.
  The remaining lemmas of the second part are steps of its proof.

Notions from other files:
* `New.LineBundle.IsHomogeneousCoords`: a vector `v` gives homogeneous coordinates of a point `t`
  for a line bundle: `v j` is a unit exactly when `t` lands in chart `j`, and there the transitions
  from chart `j` are the ratios `v k / v j`.
* `New.LineBundle.IsLinearSystem`: a line bundle whose transitions are regular on their charts,
  vanish off them, and are homogeneous coordinates of every point of the chart.
* `New.PointFn.IsRegularOn`: a function `f` is regular on an open `U`: at points `t : Spec A → X`
  that land in `U`, its value commutes with all ring maps `φ : A → B`.
* `New.Variety.AllSpecializeTo S Q`: every point of `S` specialises to the image of a point over an
  algebraically closed field with the property `Q`.
* `New.ThetaTori.ThetaTorus.IsRiemannTuple`: coefficient tuples for Riemann's relation.

modules.title: Existence of the universal theta family over a smooth projective base
modules.group: Moduli of abelian schemes embedded by theta coordinates
modules.note:
`New.Variety.ThetaNull.nonempty_universalFamily` shows, when `R` is a localization of `𝓞 E` at a
submonoid of non-zero-divisors and every maximal ideal of `R` lies over a good prime for `D`
(`IsGoodOver D R`), that the type `New.Variety.UniversalFamily D R` of universal objects is
nonempty. A universal object is a family of theta-embedded abelian schemes for the PEL data `D`
(`New.ThetaFamily`) over a projective `R`-scheme that is smooth of relative dimension
`card D.Index - 1`. Its fibres at a dense set of complex points are the theta tori
(`New.ThetaTori.ThetaTorus`) of all analytic families (`New.Variety.AnalyticFamily`). Its
uniformisations are holomorphic in the parameter and in the fibre.

The base is the reduced closure of the theta coordinates of the level points in a product of
projective spaces. `New.Variety.exists_thetaFamily_of_points` puts a family on it, using good
reduction at the level points. Smoothness comes from the immersion of the balls and the tangent
bound.

Notions from other files:
* `New.ThetaObject.TorusModel`: a model of a fibre of the family on the complex torus of a polarised
  period map, with its uniformisation and its theta functions `θ`.
* `LineBundle.IsHomogeneousCoords L t v`: `v` are homogeneous coordinates of the point `t` for `L`:
  `t` lies in the chart `j` of `L` exactly when `v j` is a unit, and there the transition function
  to the chart `k` is `v k / v j`. For a linear system (`IsLinearSystem`), the transition functions
  are regular on the charts and give homogeneous coordinates.
* `ReducedClosure`: the reduced Zariski closure `W` of a family of tuples of complex points in a
  product of schemes, with its complex points `point a`, which are dense.
* `PEL.IsGoodAt D w`: the prime `w` of `𝓞 E` is good for the data `D`: it contains neither
  `D.paddedNorm` nor the order of `D.dualTorsion`, and it contains a prime number `p` and `D.β - b`
  for an integer `b` with `D.β - b` coprime to `star D.β - b`, and two further conditions hold
  (see its definition).
modules.literature:
Known result: Moduli of abelian varieties by theta values via theta-null embedding and universal
family. Here the base is the closure of the theta values at the level points of PEL tori, not a
locus cut out by quartic relations; the family on it comes from
`New.Variety.exists_thetaFamily_of_points`. Source: D. Mumford, On the equations defining abelian
varieties II, Invent. Math. 3 (1967) 75-135; theta groups in part I, Invent. Math. 1 (1966) 287-354.

modules.title: Orthogonality of theta translates and balls of integral theta functions
modules.group: Integral theta functions and their good reduction
modules.note:
Theta functions for a full lattice `L` with Appell–Humbert data with positive Riemann form
(`New.IsPosRiemann`) are acted on by the translations `New.RealComplexForm.thetaShift B a` by the
dual lattice. The file proves an orthogonality relation for these translates. It then studies the
balls of a sup norm ‖f‖ on theta functions, built from the values at torsion points.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.IsAppellHumbert.sum_shift_mul_shift`: the orthogonality relation for the translates of two
  theta functions.
* `New.IsAppellHumbert.exists_proportional_orbit_lattice`: over a valuation ring of `ℂ`, the modules
  generated by the translates of two finite families are proportional. This needs that neither
  family is zero. It also needs a natural number that is a unit of the ring and kills the dual
  lattice modulo `L`.
* `New.ThetaTori.HasGoodReduction.normBall`: the theta functions of norm at most ‖f‖.
* `New.ThetaTori.HasGoodReduction.mem_of_mem_normBall` (from
  `New.ThetaTori.HasGoodReduction.exists_smul_thetaNorm_eq`): if f is also a theta function for an
  Appell–Humbert datum (L₀, B, ζ), L₀ ⊇ L, a module that contains the translates
  `New.RealComplexForm.thetaShift B u f` of f by the dual of L₀ contains the theta functions for
  (L₀, B, ζ) in the ball of f. The later results rest on this.
* `New.ThetaTori.HasGoodReduction.normBall_pow_pow`: if f is also a theta function for an
  Appell–Humbert datum (L₀, B, ζ) with L₀ ⊇ L/r, the r ^ j-th power of the ball of f is the ball of
  f ^ r ^ j.
* `New.ThetaTori.HasGoodReduction.finrank_reduction_eq`: the reduction of a finitely generated ball
  has dimension dim `New.RealComplexForm.thetaSpace`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.RealComplexForm.thetaShift`: The twisted translation by `a`, a complex-linear map on all
  functions `V → ℂ`: `thetaShift B a f z = exp (-(B a z + B a a / 2)) * f (z + a)`.
* `New.IsAppellHumbert`: Appell–Humbert data: Re B is symmetric, and on L one has |χ| = 1 and
  χ(l + m) = χ(l)χ(m)·exp(πi E(m, l)), E the Riemann form of B.
* `New.ThetaTori.IsAmpleType`: (L, B, χ) is an Appell–Humbert datum with positive Riemann form, and
  χ has finite order on L: χⁿ = 1 there for some n ≠ 0.
modules.literature:
Known result: Schur orthogonality for the theta group of a polarised complex torus. This is
`New.IsAppellHumbert.sum_shift_mul_shift`.

See also `Lib.Shimura.ThetaNormality.RiemannRelation` and
`Lib.Shimura.ComplexTheta.DimensionFormula`.

modules.title: Riemann's theta relation and the reduction of theta functions at a valuation
modules.group: Integral theta functions and their good reduction
modules.note:
Theta functions `θ_s = x.thetaCoord s` (`s ∈ D.dualTorsion`) of a theta torus
`x : New.ThetaTori.ThetaTorus` and their reduction at a valuation `v` of `ℂ`.

* `New.ThetaTori.ThetaTorus.isCutOutAt_reduction`: under good reduction, the ideal of the reductions
  of all theta vectors `(θ_s z)_s` has the expected ranks and is cut out by the level points.
* `New.ThetaTori.ThetaTorus.riemann_relation`: Riemann's theta relation of degree `D.paddedNorm` in
  one variable.
* `New.ThetaTori.ThetaTorus.exists_forall_valuation_thetaCoord_zero_le`: each `s` is `u + (s - u)`
  with theta constants of largest valuation.
* `New.ThetaTori.ThetaTorus.IsRiemannTuple`, `New.paddingTuple`: the systems of coefficients
  used in Riemann's relation.

Conventions: `x.torsionLift s` is a chosen lift of the torsion class `s`, `x.latticeOver S` the
lattice over a group `S` of classes, `x.intAction a` multiplication by `a ∈ 𝓞 E`, `x.multiplier` the
multiplier χ of the `θ_s`, and e(t) = exp(2πi t); `IsIntegralCoords w p` says that `p` are integral
homogeneous coordinates of a complex vector `w`, one of them a unit.

Notions from other files:
* `New.ThetaTori.ThetaTorus`: a polarised period map to `V`, with reflection matrix `ℓ`, such that
  multiplication by `star a` is adjoint to multiplication by `a ∈ 𝓞 E` for the form
  `x.automorphyForm`. In suitable coordinates `a` acts on `V` diagonally, through the complex
  embeddings of `E`.
* `New.ThetaTori.PeriodMap.thetaCoord`: The theta coordinate `θ_t`, `t ∈ T`: the normalised
  translate (`New.ThetaTori.normalizedShift`) of
  `New.ThetaTori.PeriodMap.exists_generator_thetaSpace` by the chosen lift `a_t` of `t`.
* `New.RealComplexForm.thetaShift` B a: the twisted translation f ↦ (z ↦ exp(−B(a,z) − B(a,a)/2)
  f(z + a)).
* `New.ThetaTori.LatticeForm.thetaNorm`: the supremum over torsion points x of the sizes
  `New.ThetaTori.LatticeForm.sizeAt` v(exp(−B(x,x)/2) f(x)). `New.ThetaTori.HasGoodReduction` asks,
  for an ample type on the lattice L, that this norm be multiplicative, that r > 1 and v(r) = 1, and
  that some N with v(N) = 1 multiply the dual lattice into L.
modules.literature:
Known result: Normal generation of sections on abelian varieties, kept under good reduction. Only
degrees that are powers of one integer r are treated, over a rank-one valuation ring of the complex
numbers, where powers of the sup-norm ball of theta functions are the balls and reduction keeps the
ranks. No cohomology or vanishing theorem is used. Source: S. Koizumi, Theta relations and
projective normality of abelian varieties, Amer. J. Math. 98 (1976); T. Sekiguchi, J. Math. Soc.
Japan 29 (1977) for characteristic p; G. Kempf, Multiplication over abelian varieties, Amer. J.
Math. 110 (1988).

Known result: Riemann's theta relations. Here they are stated in one variable for the theta
coordinates of a PEL torus, with multipliers in the ring of integers of a CM field in place of the
matrix with entries ±1/2. They are proved by Schur orthogonality for the theta group. Source: C.-L.
Chai, Riemann's theta formula (2014), Theorem 1.2; A. Nagano, On Riemann type relations for theta
functions on bounded symmetric domains of type I, arXiv 2301.09243 (2023), Theorem 1.1; D. Mumford,
On the equations defining abelian varieties I, Invent. Math. 1 (1966) §3; G. Kempf, Linear systems
on abelian varieties, Amer. J. Math. 111 (1989) 65–94.

modules.title: Test vectors, and the regular Hecke element that does not kill them
modules.group: Trace formula on the definite side and its comparison
modules.note:
A test vector has a cuspidal type at one split place and is spherical at another.

* `New.Variety.exists_local_hecke_element`: a Hecke element that averages against a character at one
  place.
* `New.Variety.exists_test_function`: the test function `b₁ b₀`, with `b₀` averaging against the
  type at `w₀` and `b₁` acting as a central translate of an injective operator `U_t` at `w₁`.

Conventions: `New.Variety.levelGU` is the principal level `K(𝔑)`, `New.Variety.conjAtSplit` embeds
`GL(E_w)` at a split place `w` into the adelic group, `New.Variety.GU` is the group of similitudes
of the standard form, `New.proIwahori` is the pro-p Iwahori subgroup, and `New.Variety.heckeAlgebra`
is the Hecke algebra inside the group ring, acting through `asAlgebraHom`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.SplitFinPlace`: The finite places w of E with w̄ ≠ w, that is, those split over the
  maximal real subfield.
* `New.Variety.IsRegularHecke`: f is regular if f(x⁻¹y⁻¹x) ≠ 0, with y in GL_n(E) and x adelic,
  forces the characteristic polynomial of y to be separable.
* `New.Variety.dualComponent`: The inverse transpose of the component at a split place; a left
  inverse of `New.Variety.conjAtSplit`.
* `New.iwahoriHeckeHom`: t ↦ U_t, the mean over `New.proIwahori` composed with the action of a
  dominant diagonal t, on the vectors fixed by `New.proIwahori`.
* `New.Variety.GUPlus`: The monoid of similitudes `g` whose inverse has integral entries, that is,
  which enlarge the standard lattice.

modules.title: Trace formula for algebraic forms, finiteness of signed frame classes, the definite side
modules.group: Trace formula on the definite side and its comparison
modules.note:
This file gives a trace formula for a Hecke operator on a finite-dimensional space of algebraic
forms, computed from class representatives with weights. It also shows that only finitely many
double cosets GL_n(E) x (GU ∩ V), with V an open subgroup, contain a signed frame. These results
serve the definite side of the comparison of traces. There the trace of a regular Hecke element on
forms supported on definite frames is written as a sum over orbits of triples.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.trace_eq_weighted_sum`: the trace of the twisted Hecke operator `T` on a finite-dimensional
  space of algebraic forms, from representatives `r i` with weights `w i`.
* `New.Variety.finite_isSignedFrame_classes`: for an open subgroup V, only finitely many double
  cosets GL_n(E) x (GU ∩ V) contain a signed frame.
* `New.Variety.definiteForms`: the forms with values in a representation `ξ` of `GL n E` that
  are left `GL n E`-equivariant, vanish off the definite frames and are right invariant under the
  level.
* `New.Variety.definiteForms.rep`: the action of the Hecke algebra `New.Variety.heckeAlgebra` on it.
* `New.Variety.finite_definiteForms`, `New.Variety.finite_support_countTerm_definite`,
  `New.Variety.trace_definiteForms_eq_finsum_countTerm`: finite dimension, finite support and the
  trace formula.

Notions from other files:
* `New.levelSpace π K`: The vectors fixed by the subgroup `K` under the representation `π`; here
  `π` is `New.rightRegular`, the action of `G` on functions `G → W` by right translation.
* `New.Variety.GU`: The unitary similitudes: the `g ∈ GL_n(𝔸f E)` with `c • gᴴ g = ε • 1` for some
  rational `c > 0` and unit `ε` of `Ẑ`, that is, the frames of the forms `c • 1`.
* `New.Variety.levelGU`: the principal level K(𝔑), the similitudes in `GL_n(Ô E)` that are congruent
  to `1` modulo `𝔑`.
* `New.Variety.IsRegularHecke`: a(x⁻¹y⁻¹xK) ≠ 0 forces the characteristic polynomial of `y` to
  be separable.
* `New.Variety.IsNeat`: The level 𝔑 is neat: 𝔑 ≠ 0 and, whenever `x` is a signed frame with `ℓ` for
  some form (`New.Variety.IsSignedFrame`), every y in GL_n(E) with x⁻¹yx in `levelGU n 𝔑` that fixes
  ℓ under `New.Variety.ratConj` equals 1.

modules.title: For a function with a cuspidal type at one place, marked and definite orbit sums agree
modules.group: Trace formula on the definite side and its comparison
modules.note:
* `New.Variety.finsum_orbits_eq_zero_of_free_of_blocks`: a sum over orbits vanishes if it vanishes
  on each block of a partition that the group permutes, with finite support there, and the
  stabiliser of each point where it is non-zero is trivial.
* `New.Variety.finsum_markedTerm_eq_finsum_definiteTerm`: the marked and the definite sums agree for
  every weight; `New.Variety.finsum_countTerm_marked_eq_definite` says this in terms of `countTerm`.

Idea: both sums run over the classes of triples `(xK, y, μ)` under `GL n E`. Classes with
