irreducible characteristic polynomial are matched by a change of signs. For a reducible one, an
idempotent at the split place gives a unipotent group, whose orbits cut the triples into blocks;
translation along it multiplies the terms by a value of the character that is not 1, so they sum to
zero on each block.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.MarkedTriple`: triples `(xK, y, μ)` of an adelic coset, an element `y` of `GL n E`
  and an index `μ` of an eigenvalue of `y`.
* `New.Variety.countTerm`: the term `f(x⁻¹ y⁻¹ x K) * u(charpoly y, μ)` of the class of
  `(xK, y, μ)` if `IsSignedFrame x (eigenReflection ε y μ)` holds (the sign condition), else `0`;
  `ε = True` gives the marked count and `ε = False` the definite count.
* `New.Variety.conjAtSplit`: places an element of `GL n` over the completion at a split place `w₀`
  in the adelic similitude group; `New.Variety.dualComponent` is a left inverse.
* `New.Variety.IsRegularHecke`: `f(x⁻¹ y⁻¹ x K) ≠ 0` forces the characteristic polynomial of `y` to
  be separable.
* `New.Variety.IsCuspidalType`: for every idempotent matrix `e ≠ 0, 1`, the character `χ` is
  non-trivial on the elements of `J` in the unipotent group `1 + e M_n (1 - e)`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Simple trace formula on a definite group, with vanishing non-elliptic terms. This
file proves the comparison of orbit sums that is used, for unitary similitudes at a neat level, with
Haar integrals replaced by finite sums over cosets. The non-elliptic terms cancel for a regular test
function with a cuspidal type at one split place; the elliptic terms match for n odd.
Source: Dummigan, A simple trace formula for algebraic modular forms, Exp. Math. 22 (2013); Arthur
and Clozel, Simple algebras, base change and the advanced theory of the trace formula (1989), ch. 1
§2, after Deligne and Kazhdan.

modules.title: Eigenline reflections of a separable matrix, and the term of the count at a marked triple
modules.group: Transfer of Hecke eigensystems via the Lefschetz formula
modules.note:
Invariance properties of the terms of the point count `New.Variety.countTerm`, a function on
GL_n(E)-orbits of triples (coset xK, rational matrix y, index μ of a root), the type
`MarkedTriple (levelGU n 𝔑) n`.

* `New.Variety.isReflection_markedReflection` and
  `New.Variety.exists_eq_markedReflection_iff_of_ratConj_eq` (bundled as
  `New.Variety.isReflection_markedReflection_and_exists_eq_iff`): for y with separable
  characteristic polynomial, the matrices `New.Variety.markedReflection y i` are reflections, and
  each reflection that commutes with y equals exactly one of them.
* `New.Variety.countTerm_mk`: the term of an orbit may be computed at any representative.
* `New.Variety.finsum_countTerm_eq_sum`: the weighted count as a finite sum over the support of the
  count of weight 1.

`New.Variety.IsReflection J` says J = u wᵀ - 1 with w · u = 2. `New.Variety.ratConj z` conjugates by
Φ_{v₀}(z), the image of z in GL_n(ℂ) under the fixed embedding Φ v₀ : E → ℂ used throughout.
`New.Variety.IsSignedFrame x J` says that x is a frame for a rational form whose signature is given
by J.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.heckeAlgebra`: the Hecke algebra of level K(𝔑): the subalgebra of elements ∑ a_g [g]
  of ℂ[GL_n(𝔸_f)] that are supported on `GUPlus E n` and whose function ∑ a_g 1_{gK} is left
  K(𝔑)-invariant.
* `New.Variety.levelGU`: the principal level K(𝔑), the similitudes in `GL_n(Ô E)` that are congruent
  to `1` modulo `𝔑`.
* `New.Variety.toFinGL`: The diagonal embedding of GL_n(E) in GL_n of the finite adeles of E.
* `New.Variety.heckeCosetFn f`: for f = ∑ a_g [g] in the Hecke algebra, the function ∑ a_g 1_{gK} on
  the cosets of the level `K`.
* `New.Variety.eigenReflection ε y μ`: if `ε` holds, the matrix `New.Variety.markedReflection y μ`,
  a polynomial in Φ_{v₀}(y) that is `1` on the eigenline of the `μ`-th listed root of the
  characteristic polynomial and `-1` on the other eigenlines; if `ε` fails, the identity.

modules.title: h-null Hecke elements and the Lefschetz formula as a sum over marked pairs
modules.group: Transfer of Hecke eigensystems via the Lefschetz formula
modules.note:
Translates the geometric vanishing of local terms on a tower of Kuga–Sato varieties into a vanishing
of a sum over marked pairs, which involves only the Hecke function.

* `New.Variety.IsNullHecke`: h-nullity of a Hecke element, a condition on regular elements.
* `New.Variety.OccursInWeight`: a system of eigenvalues θ occurs in weight h.
* `New.Variety.Model.isNullHecke_of_isNullFamily`: h-null on deep levels of the tower implies
  h-null.

Idea: coincidences of two maps to the base are grouped by their marked pair; each fibre has (number
of lattice solutions) · (order of the deck group) points, and the number of solutions cancels the
denominator of the local term.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.GUPlus`: the monoid of similitudes `g` whose inverse has integral entries, that is,
  which enlarge the standard lattice.
* `New.Variety.heckeAlgebra`: the Hecke algebra, the subalgebra of elements ∑ a_g [g] of k[G]
  supported on `GUPlus E n` whose function ∑ a_g 1_{g·levelGU n 𝔑} is left `levelGU n 𝔑`-invariant.
* `New.Variety.levelGU`: the principal level K(𝔑), the similitudes in `GL_n(Ô E)` that are congruent
  to `1` modulo `𝔑`.
* `New.Variety.Model`: the tower of Kuga–Sato varieties over `R`, given by a list of properties.
* `New.Variety.IsNeat`: the level 𝔑 is neat: 𝔑 ≠ 0 and, whenever `x` is a signed frame with `ℓ` for
  some form (`New.Variety.IsSignedFrame`), every y in GL_n(E) with x⁻¹yx in `levelGU n 𝔑` that fixes
  ℓ under `New.Variety.ratConj` equals 1.

modules.title: Coefficient systems from weights and the degrees where Hecke eigensystems occur
modules.group: Transfer of Hecke eigensystems via the Lefschetz formula
modules.note:
A weight `κ` gives a coefficient system on `GL_a(E)`. Its Hecke eigensystems occur in the degrees
given by the jumps of `κ`, in the sense of `New.Variety.OccursInWeight`: the local terms of the
Lefschetz side do not all cancel.

`Φ v` is the embedding that the CM type chooses at `v`, and `v₀` is the base infinite place fixed by
`New.CMBase E`.

* `New.Variety.occursInWeight_of_isTestEigenform`: the Hecke eigenvalues of a test eigenform occur,
  if the character of the coefficients is given by a Schur polynomial and powers of the determinant.
* `New.Variety.exists_isCoefficientSystem`: the coefficient system attached to a weight, and the
  occurrence of the eigensystems of its test vectors.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Weight`: For `κ : Weight E` and an infinite place `v` of `E`, `κ.1 v h` is the number of
  columns of height `h` of a Young diagram, and `κ.2 v` is an integer exponent of the determinant.
* `New.Variety.entryConj`: The endomorphism of the unitary group {g : gᴴg = 1} of matrices over R
  indexed by `n` that applies the involution of R to each entry.
* `New.jumps`: The multiset {j − 1 − λ_j} if σ is in the CM type, else {λ_j + a − j}, 1 ≤ j ≤ a,
  with λ the highest weight of κ at σ.
* `New.Space.weightRep`: The representation of the rational unitary group on coordinate vectors of
  weight `(κ.1, κ.2)`, through its components at the infinite places and `New.conjWeylRep`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Transfer of eigensystems between unitary inner forms differing at a real place. Only
the occurrence is proved here, namely that the Hecke eigensystem of a definite form occurs, in each
Hodge weight, on the variety for signature (1, n-1), with n odd and a cuspidal type at one split
place. It is proved by comparing two finite counts, without stabilisation. Source: Harris and
Labesse, Conditional base change for unitary groups, Asian J. Math. 8 (2004), Thm 2.1.2; Labesse,
Changement de base CM et séries discrètes (2011), Thm 5.4; count as in Goresky and MacPherson, The
topological trace formula (2003), and Shimura, On the trace formula for Hecke operators, Acta Math.
132 (1974).

modules.title: Adelic frames over a CM field, torsion classes, period lattices and period maps
modules.group: Complex uniformisation of abelian varieties and moduli points
modules.note:
This file develops the linear algebra over a CM field `E` used to count points. `New.CMBase E` fixes
a CM type `Φ` and a base infinite place `v₀`, where the signature condition is imposed.
`New.AdelicTorsion E n` is `(𝔸f E / Ô E)ⁿ`, an adelic model of `(E / 𝓞 E)ⁿ`. Here `𝔸f E` is the ring
of finite adeles and `Ô E` the ring of integral finite adeles. `New.Variety.torsionClass` is the
class map. Adelic frames give lattices of rational vectors in `(E ⊗ ℝ)ⁿ`, which are shown to be
discrete and full. A complex matrix gives a complex structure on this space.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.IsFrameFor β x`: `xᴴ β x` is a scalar matrix `ε • 1` with `ε` a unit of `Ẑ = Ô ℚ`.
* `New.Variety.IsSignedFrame x J`: `x` is a frame of some `β` that is positive definite at every
  infinite place other than `v₀`, with `β J` positive definite at `v₀`.
* `New.Variety.ModuliPoint`: points `(x, J, P)` at infinite level, with the action
  `New.Variety.ModuliPoint.act` and the isomorphisms `New.Variety.ModuliPoint.IsLevelIso` at a level
  `K`.
* `New.Variety.IsPeriodMap`: a map onto a complex vector space that carries the complex structure
  `i J` at `v₀` and `i` at the other infinite places to multiplication by `i`.
* `New.Variety.exists_matrix_torsionClass_eq`: an `𝓞 E`-linear map `Eⁿ → AdelicTorsion E n` is
  `y ↦ torsionClass (h y)` for an adelic matrix `h`, found by compactness of `Ô`.

Notions from other files:
* `𝔸f E`, `Ô E`: the finite adeles of `E` and the integral ones (the product of the completions of
  `𝓞 E`); `finAdeleIncl ℚ E` maps the finite adeles of `ℚ` into those of `E`.
* `New.CMType E`: a CM type, a complex embedding `Φ w` for every infinite place `w` of `E`;
  `FinComplexSpace V`: `V` is a finite-dimensional complex vector space with its topology.

modules.title: Holomorphic families of complex points, jets, uniformisations and theta coordinates
modules.group: Complex uniformisation of abelian varieties and moduli points
modules.note:
Except in `New.Uniformisation.hasSignature_iff`, where `O` is any commutative ring acting on `A`,
`O` is a valuation ring with fraction field `ℂ` (`New.ValuativeArc`), for example `ℂ` itself. This
file develops calculus for families of complex points of schemes over `O` without an
analytification: holomorphic families, jets and a chain rule. These notions are applied to a
uniformisation `V / L ≅ A(O)` of a commutative group scheme `A`, which yields a count of its torsion
points. The file also treats linear systems whose homogeneous coordinates are theta functions, and
their behaviour under operations on line bundles.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.HolomorphicAt.exists_isJet`, `New.IsJet.unique`, `New.isJet_comp_iff`: jets exist and are
  unique, and they obey the chain rule.
* `New.HolomorphicAt.isFirstOrderConst_of_nsmul`: on a smooth commutative group scheme, if `n • φ`
  is constant to first order in a direction, for some `n ≠ 0`, then so is `φ`.
* `New.Uniformisation.hasSignature_iff`: the condition `New.HasSignature` on the matrices of the
  action of `O` in algebraic coordinates holds iff the space `V` of a uniformisation has a common
  eigenvector `Y ≠ 0` of the maps `F a`, with eigenvalues `ρ a`, such that `F b - ρ c` maps `V` into
  the line of `Y`.
* `New.Uniformisation.card_torsion`: A(O) has m^(2 dim V) points killed by m ≠ 0.
* `New.HasThetaCoords.pull`, `New.HasThetaCoords.pow`, `New.HasThetaCoords.pull_translate`,
  `New.HasThetaCoords.mul`: pull-back, power, translation and tensor product.
* `New.HasThetaCoords.riemannForm_eq_of_isFrame`: if `N ⊗ M⁻¹` has a frame, the Riemann forms and
  the multipliers of `N` and `M` agree, and along the family the frame is a constant times
  exp((B − B′)(z, z)/2)·θ′/θ.

Notions from other files:
* `New.PointFn`: a function on the points of a scheme X; it assigns to each point Spec R → X, for
  every ring R, an element of R, with no compatibility required.
* `New.LandsIn`: the point t : Spec R → X lands in the open U when all of Spec R maps into U.
* `New.IsAppellHumbert`: Appell–Humbert data (B, χ) for a lattice L: Re B is symmetric, and on L one
  has |χ| = 1 and χ(l + m) = χ(l)χ(m)·exp(πi E(m, l)), where E(u, v) = Im(B(u, v) − B(v, u))/(2π) is
  the Riemann form of B (`New.RealComplexForm.riemannForm`).
* `New.RealComplexForm.thetaSpace`: the entire functions f on V with f(z + l) = χ(l)·exp(B(l,
  z) + B(l, l)/2)·f(z) for l in L.
* `New.LineBundle.IsHomogeneousCoords`, `New.LineBundle.IsLinearSystem`: v is a vector of
  homogeneous coordinates of the point t for the line bundle N when t lands in the chart U_j exactly
  when v_j is a unit, and then g_jk(t) = v_k/v_j. N is a linear system when each transition function
  g_ij is regular on U_i and zero at the points outside U_i, and the g_ij(t), j varying, are
  homogeneous coordinates of every point t of U_i.

modules.title: Existence in Appell–Humbert: projective embeddings are given by theta functions
modules.group: Complex uniformisation of abelian varieties and moduli points
modules.note:
The existence half of the Appell–Humbert theorem, for a projective embedding N of a uniformised
group A(ℂ) = V/L whose class satisfies the parallelogram law.

* `New.Uniformisation.appell_humbert`: the coordinates of N are theta functions for some
  Appell–Humbert data (L, B, χ) with positive Riemann form.
* `New.exists_analyticAt_double_eq`, `New.exists_extension_double`, `New.induction_on_double`: the
  doubling equation near 0, and its continuation to the whole space by halving.

Idea: the parallelogram law gives a frame on A × A, and its values define a function c. After
multiplying c by exp q(z, z) for a suitable quadratic form q, the doubling equation
σ(2z) = σ(z)⁴c(z) is solved near 0 and continued to V by halving. Then σ trivialises the pullback of
N.

`New.Uniformisation` A V is a surjective homomorphism e = `u.expMap` : V → A(ℂ), holomorphic and
immersive, with kernel the lattice L = `u.lattice`. `New.HasThetaCoords` says that θ(z) gives
homogeneous coordinates of e(z), each θ_i a theta function of type (B, χ): entire, with
θ_i(z + l) = χ(l)·exp(B l z + B l l / 2)·θ_i(z) for l in L.

Notions from other files:
* `New.atGeneric`: For a family s of sections of A over Spec O, O a valuation ring of ℂ, the complex
  point of A given by s(z) at the generic point.
* `New.LineBundle.IsHomogeneousCoords`: v is a vector of homogeneous coordinates of the point t for
  L: t lands in U_j exactly when v_j is a unit, and then g_jk(t) = v_k/v_j.
* `New.IsAppellHumbert`: Re B is symmetric, and on L one has |χ| = 1 and χ(l + m) = χ(l)χ(m)·exp(πi
  E(m, l)), E the Riemann form of B.
* `New.IsPosRiemann`: The Riemann form E of B is positive: E(u, iu) > 0 for every u ≠ 0.
* `New.Pic.ParallelogramLaw`: The parallelogram law for a class c in Pic A:
  (x+y)^*c + (x−y)^*c + 2·0^*c = 2(x^*c + y^*c) in Pic T for all T-points x, y of A and all
  S-schemes T.
modules.literature:
Known result: Appell–Humbert theorem, a step in the complex uniformisation of PEL abelian varieties.
For a given uniformisation, this file proves the existence half, for a very ample class obeying the
parallelogram law. Source: J. S. Milne, Introduction to Shimura Varieties (2005/2017), Theorem 8.17
and Lemma 5.12; R. Kottwitz, Points on some Shimura varieties over finite fields, J. AMS 5 (1992)
§8; G. Shimura, On analytic families of polarized abelian varieties and automorphic functions, Ann.
Math. 78 (1963); A. Borel, Some finiteness properties of adele groups over number fields, Publ. IHES
16 (1963); D. Mumford, Abelian Varieties §§1–2; L. Breen, Fonctions thêta et théorème du cube, LNM
980 (1983).

modules.title: Exponential of compact commutative Lie groups and uniformisation of abelian varieties
modules.group: Complex uniformisation of abelian varieties and moduli points
modules.note:
The complex points `New.ComplexPoint A` of a scheme `A` over ℂ carry the classical topology. Here
`A` is an object of `Over (Spec ℂ)`, and a point is a morphism from `Spec ℂ` over it. A smooth
scheme has holomorphic charts, and a projective variety has compact complex points. For an abelian
variety A with a projective embedding (`New.LineBundle.IsProjEmbedding`), the group A(ℂ) is
therefore compact and commutative with a holomorphic chart at 0. An exponential map exists for any
such group, and it gives a uniformisation of A by ℂᵈ, where d is the dimension of A.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_lie_exponential` constructs the exponential map of a compact commutative group with a
  chart at `0` in which addition is complex analytic. The value at `v` is a limit of `n • ψ (v / n)`
  along an ultrafilter on `ℕ`, which exists by compactness; no differential equation is solved.
* `New.exists_holomorphic_chart`: a smooth scheme has a holomorphic chart at every complex point.
* `New.LineBundle.IsProjEmbedding.compactSpace_complexPoint`: the complex points of a projective
  variety are compact.
* `New.LineBundle.IsProjEmbedding.nonempty_uniformisation`: an abelian variety of dimension d is
  uniformised by ℂᵈ.

Notions from other files:
* `New.IsFullRankLattice L`: the `ℤ`-submodule `L` of `V` is discrete and spans `V` over `ℝ`. Here
  `V` is a `FinComplexSpace`, that is, a finite-dimensional complex normed space.
* `New.IsAbelianScheme`: a commutative group scheme A over S is abelian if it is smooth and proper
  over S and multiplication by every m ≠ 0 is surjective.
* `New.Uniformisation`: a surjective homomorphism from a complex vector space V to the complex
  points of A, with kernel a lattice, holomorphic and immersive, through which homomorphisms
  holomorphic at 0 factor ℂ-linearly.
* `New.LineBundle.IsProjEmbedding`: The linear system N embeds the proper scheme X in projective
  space: points in one chart with the same affine coordinates and the same base point are equal.
* `New.HasGermAt`: For each open U of X containing φ(w₀) and each f regular on U: φ(w) lies in U for
  w near w₀, and the function f∘φ satisfies Q. `New.HolomorphicAt` is the case where Q is
  analyticity at w₀.

modules.title: Period signatures, analytic families of theta tori and the ball chart of moduli points
modules.group: Complex uniformisation of abelian varieties and moduli points
modules.note:
Φ v denotes the embedding E → ℂ that the CM type chooses at the infinite place v, and v₀ is the base
infinite place fixed by `New.CMBase`. Theta tori that vary analytically with a parameter b in a
domain of ℂⁿ⁻¹, all uniformised by one fixed space V, form analytic families. Near each b₀, their
theta coordinates become analytic after a common factor c(b) ≠ 0. For a fixed frame, the positive
lines form a ball, and the moduli points with this frame are the points of a single analytic family
over that ball.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.ThetaTori.PeriodMap.isSignedFrameFor`: the sign condition on the matrix of a polarised period
  map.
* `New.Variety.AnalyticFamily`: a family of theta tori, with periods Q_b analytic in b and with
  B(Q_b ·, ·) independent of b.
* `New.Variety.AnalyticFamily.exists_analytic_thetaCoord`: near b₀, after a common factor c(b) ≠ 0,
  the theta coordinates are analytic in (b, z).
* `New.Variety.positiveBall`, `New.Variety.exists_ball_chart`: the positive lines, in coordinates
  ℂ × ℂ^(n−1); the set is star-convex, hence connected.
* `New.Variety.ballPeriod`: an explicit period map (E ⊗ ℝ)ⁿ → `New.Variety.BallFibre`, affine in the
  point.
* `New.Variety.exists_analyticFamily_positiveBall`: the ball carries an analytic family
  `New.Variety.AnalyticFamily` with these periods and the reflections `New.Variety.formReflection`.
* `New.Variety.IsBallFamily`, `New.Variety.exists_isBallFamily`: the points with the frame of a
  given point o are the points `New.Variety.AnalyticFamily.ballPoint` of one analytic family. An
  isomorphism z in GL_n(E) from a translate o·(g, α) to o acts on the parameters near 0 by a linear
  map K, and its local term, a complex polynomial p (`New.Variety.localTerm`), satisfies
  p(t) = p(0)·det(1 − tK) for all t in ℂ.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.IsSignedFrameFor` g ℓ β: the adelic matrix `g` is a frame for the matrix `β` over E,
  the matrix `β.map (Φ w)` is positive definite for every infinite place `w ≠ v₀`, and
  `β.map (Φ v₀) * ℓ` is positive definite.
* `New.Variety.IsPeriodMap` ℓ Q: Q carries iℓ at v₀ and i at the other places to multiplication by
  i.
* `New.Variety.BallBase`: The complex vector space ℂ^(n−1), which contains the parameter domains of
  the families of periods.
* `New.Variety.RealVectors`: The space (E ⊗ ℝ)ⁿ, written as n-tuples of elements of the product of
  copies of ℂ over the infinite places of E.
* `New.Variety.BallFibre`: The complex space (ℂ × ℂ^(n−1)) × ∏_{v ≠ v₀} ℂⁿ, the common target of the
  period maps of a family.

modules.title: Objects modelled on complex tori and their homomorphisms as rational matrices
modules.group: Complex uniformisation of abelian varieties and moduli points
modules.note:
This file models the objects of a PEL family `X` (`New.ThetaFamily`) over a valuation ring with
fraction field ℂ on complex tori `V` modulo a lattice given by a polarised period map. It then
describes homomorphisms of modelled objects by matrices `z ∈ GL_n(E)`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.ThetaObject.TorusModel`: `y.groupScheme` is uniformised by `V` modulo that lattice, with
  theta coordinates.
* `New.ThetaTori.PeriodMap.exists_uniformisation_of_isSeparatingFamily`: a dense map given by theta
  functions is a uniformisation.
* `New.ThetaObject.TorusModel.fullStructure`: a model trivialises all torsion, compatibly with the
  Weil pairing. `New.ThetaObject.TorusModel.exists_unit_on_roots_of_unity` supplies the unit of Ẑ
  through which a ring homomorphism `O → ℂ` acts on roots of unity.
* `New.ThetaObject.TorusModel.exists_isTranslationLift_of_dualLattice` (with its parts
  `New.ThetaObject.TorusModel.card_nsmul_mem_of_mem_dualLattice` and
  `New.ThetaObject.TorusModel.exists_isTranslationLift_of_mem_dualLattice`),
  `New.ThetaObject.TorusModel.multiplier_eq_canonicalMultiplier`: translations by the dual lattice
  lift to `y.lineBundle`, and the multiplier of the theta coordinates is the canonical one.
* `New.ThetaObject.TorusModel.exists_matrix_of_hom`: a linear `ψ` of multiplier `μ ≠ 0` comes from a
  `z`.
* `New.ThetaObject.TorusModel.exists_isIsogenyOfMatrix`,
  `New.ThetaObject.TorusModel.exists_isogeny`: a `z` with `z ℓ z⁻¹ = ℓ'` and `g'⁻¹ z g` an integral
  similitude of multiplier `μ` gives an isogeny (`New.ThetaObject.TorusModel.IsIsogenyOfMatrix`);
  objects with models have the same map from `𝓞 E`
  (`New.ThetaObject.TorusModel.baseHom_eq_baseHom`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.ThetaTori.PeriodMap`: the linear part of a model: a real isomorphism Q from (E ⊗ ℝ)ⁿ onto V,
  a form β with frame g, and a form B on V whose Riemann form pulls back to
  `New.Variety.polarisationForm`.
* `New.Variety.frameCoords`: the map y ↦ g⁻¹y from Eⁿ to n-tuples of finite adeles.
* `New.Variety.realVecAction`: the action of a matrix A over E on (E ⊗ ℝ)ⁿ, through Φ_v(A) at the
  infinite place v.

modules.title: Every full complex object is modelled on a point (g, ℓ)
modules.group: Complex uniformisation of abelian varieties and moduli points
modules.note:
From a complex point of a family of abelian schemes back to linear algebra: an object `x` over `ℂ`
with structure map `Φ v₀` (the complex embedding of `E` at the fixed infinite place `v₀`) on `𝓞 E`
and a full structure `e` (a trivialisation of all torsion, `New.ThetaObject.FullLevelStructure`) is
a complex torus described by an adelic frame `g` and a reflection `ℓ`.

* `New.Variety.exists_torusModel`: a polarised period map on `ℂ^d` for `(g, ℓ)` and a model of `x`
  on it whose torsion points are those of `e`, with `ℓ` a reflection.
* `New.Variety.exists_torusModel_of_isPeriodMap`: the same model on a given period map `Q` whose
  exponential lifts the torsion points of `e`; the frame is found from the Weil pairing of `e`.

`New.ThetaObject.TorusModel` is a model of `x` on a given polarised period map `Q`
(`New.ThetaTori.PeriodMap`). It is a uniformisation of `x.groupScheme` whose kernel is the period
lattice.

Notions from other files:
* `New.ψf`: the additive character of the finite adeles with ψ_f(x) = exp(2πi Tr_{E/ℚ}(a)) for any a
  in E with x − a integral. In the code `𝐞 t` is exp(2πi t).
* `New.ThetaObject.groupScheme`: The group scheme with O_E-action of an object x over S: the
  pull-back of the abelian scheme of the family along x : S → base.
* `New.ThetaObject.baseHom`: For an object x over Spec R, the ring homomorphism O_E → R induced by x
  and the structure morphism of the base of the family to Spec O_E.
* `New.ThetaObject`: An object of the family X over a scheme T: a morphism from T to the base of X.
